Mahogho viya sassāni, vināsenti tapoguṇaṃ.

Having become like a thorny waste of the mind, entangled with bonds; like a great flood destroying crops, they destroy the quality of asceticism.

1005.

1005.

Visayassādavikkhittā, vikiṇṇā pākatindriyā;

Muṭṭhassatī kusītā ca, jīvanti moghajīvitaṃ.

Distracted by the taste of sense objects, with faculties uncontrolled; with lost mindfulness and lazy, they live a vain life.

1006.

1006.

Mahagghasā bāhulikā, duppaññā kāyadaḷhikā;

Ganthanīvaraṇābaddhā, icchālobhavasīkatā.

Gluttonous, indulgent, unwise, physically obstinate; bound by ties and hindrances, mastered by craving and greed.

1007.

1007.

Malaggahitasantānā, tiracchānakathāratā;

Vinayopasamāpetā, visamācāragocarā.

Their stream of being seized by defilements, delighting in animal talk; devoid of the calming of discipline, their range is unrighteous conduct.

1008.

1008.

Dubbharatā ca dupposā, sukumārasukhālayā;

Asantuṭṭhā mahicchā ca, loluppācāralakkhitā.

Hard to support and hard to nourish, dwelling in delicate pleasures; discontented and of great desire, marked by greedy conduct.

1009.

1009.

Duggandheneva sunakhā, āmagandhena mucchitā;

Tattha tatthābhidhāvantā, na patiṭṭhanti sāsane.

Like dogs infatuated by a foul odor, by the scent of raw flesh, running hither and thither, they find no footing in the Dispensation.

1010.

1010.

Nillajjā [M 0.0086] vītasārajjā, lokadhammesu mucchitā;

Pāpicchā kuhanacchannā, micchājīvapalobhitā.

Shameless, without modesty, infatuated with worldly conditions; with evil desires, covered by deceit, lured by wrong livelihood.

1011.

1011.

Saṭhā [V 0.0092] pagabbhā māyāvī, antopūti avassutā;

Saṅkassarasamācārā, kasambu sithilā jaḷā.

Cunning, insolent, deceitful, rotten within, depraved; of coarse behavior, stained, lax, and dull.

1012.

1012.

Siṅgāracapalācittā, pūtikāyānurāgino;

Sīdantā palimāpannā, na viruḷhanti sāsane.

With minds amorous and fickle, attached to foul bodies; sinking, mired, they do not grow in the Dispensation.

1013.

1013.

Pāpapuggalasaṃsaṭṭhā, pāpadiṭṭhiparāgatā;

Asaddhā dhammanicchinnā, duṭṭhā dubbacaniṭṭhurā.

Associating with wicked people, given over to wrong views; faithless, cut off from the Dhamma, corrupt, hard to admonish, and cruel.

1014.

1014.

Sāmaññaṃ paridhaṃsentā, dūsentā jinasāsanaṃ;

Atikkamma jinovādaṃ, bālā duggatibhāgino.

Disparaging the ascetic life, defiling the Victor’s Dispensation; transgressing the Victor’s instruction, fools are destined for a woeful state.

1015.

1015.

Kāmagiddhā durācārā, dussīlā mohapārutā;

Khajjantā kaddamībhūtā, jinasāsanakaṇṭakā.

Greedy for sensual pleasures, of bad conduct, immoral, shrouded in delusion; being consumed, having become like mire—thorns in the Conqueror's Dispensation.

1016.

1016.

Hitāhitamajānantā, anurodhavirodhino;

Cetopahatasantānā, vipallāsapalambhitā.

Not knowing what is beneficial and harmful, prone to compliance and opposition; their mental continuities afflicted, deceived by distortions.

1017.

1017.

Vipannākulakammantā, pāpakārī parājitā;

Socanti dīghamaddhānaṃ, apāyamhi samappitā.

With failed and confused undertakings, doers of evil, defeated; they sorrow for a long time, consigned to the states of woe.

1018.

1018.

Itthaṃ hitasamucchedī, kumaggoyaṃ rajāpatho;

Pāpadhammappavattīti, viditvā puna paṇḍito.

Thus, this wrong way, this path of defilement, is destructive of what is beneficial. Knowing this to be the practice of evil qualities, the wise one turns away.

1019.

1019.

Pariyuṭṭhānasaṃklesaṃ, vippharantaṃ visārado;

Paṭisaṅkhāya rundheyya, manteneva mahāvisaṃ.

The spreading defilements of obsession—the skilled one, reflecting, should restrain them, as one would a great poison with a spell.

1020.

1020.

Khippamādittacelova, pāpapāvakamuṭṭhitaṃ;

Bhāvanājalasekena, nibbāpeyya nirantaraṃ.

Like one whose garment is ablaze, one should quickly and unceasingly extinguish the arisen fire of evil with the water of meditative development.

1021.

1021.

Appamādena medhāvī, nageneva mahānadiṃ;

Pāpoghaṃ paṭibandhanto, pidaheyya khaṇe khaṇe.

The wise one, with diligence, obstructing the flood of evil as a mountain does a great river, should block it moment by moment.

1022.

1022.

Sabhayaṃ [M 0.0087] viya kantāraṃ, ghoramāsīvisaṃ yathā;

Papātamiva gambhīraṃ, miḷhaṃ viya ca paṇḍito.

The wise one regards it as a fearful wilderness, as a deadly viper, as a deep precipice, and as filth.

1023.

1023.

Pahāya [V 0.0093] pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, nekkhammamadhimuccati;

Kalyāṇamitto vajjesu, bhayadassāvi subbato.

Having abandoned obsession, one is resolved on renunciation; a spiritual friend, seeing danger in faults, is of good vows.

1024.

1024.

Kāmarāgavisaṃyutto, bhogadhananirālayo;

Icchālobhavinimutto, amamo apariggaho.

Disjoined from sensual lust, unattached to possessions and wealth; liberated from desire and greed, without possessiveness, not grasping.

1025.

1025.

Sorato sakhilo saṇho, mettāyanto dayāparo;

Anāhaṭamano dhīro, santacitto khamāparo.

Gentle, friendly, and tender, extending loving-kindness, compassionate; with mind undefiled, steadfast, with mind serene, and forbearing.

1026.

1026.

Hitesī sabbapāṇīnaṃ,

Issāmaccheramuccito;

Kodhopanāhabyāpāda

Virodhopasame rato.

Seeking the welfare of all beings, freed from envy and stinginess; delighting in the calming of anger, resentment, ill will, and opposition.

1027.

1027.

Anolīnamano yogī, niccāraddhaparakkamo;

Susamāhitasaṅkappo, vippasanno anāvilo.

The yogi, with mind unadhering, ever putting forth effort; with well-composed intention, serene, and unperturbed.

1028.

1028.

Okappento vimuccanto, paññavā paṭipattiyaṃ;

Pihayanto mamāyanto, sammāsambuddhasāsanaṃ.

Trusting and becoming liberated, wise in practice; aspiring to and cherishing the Dispensation of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

1029.

1029.

Iti nīvaraṇāpeto, ñāṇālokajutindharo;

Pūjeti sammāsambuddhaṃ, saddhammapaṭipattiyā.

Thus, rid of hindrances, bearing the radiant light of wisdom, one honors the Perfectly Enlightened One through the practice of the true Dhamma.

1030.

1030.

Hirottappaguṇopeto,

Kalyāṇācāragocaro;

Makkhappalāsarahito,

Sappatisso sagāravo.

Endowed with the qualities of moral shame and fear of wrongdoing, whose range is virtuous conduct; free from denigration and arrogance, respectful, reverent.

1031.

1031.

Ajjavācāracāritto, māyāsāṭheyyanissaṭo;

Thambhasārambhanissaṅgo, maddavācārapesalo.

Of straightforward conduct and character, devoid of deceit and trickery; free from obstinacy and arrogance, gentle in conduct and amiable.

1032.

1032.

Mānātimānavimukho[M 0.0088], saddhammagarusādaro;

Parappamādanimmaddī, saṃvegabahulo sadā.

Free from pride and conceit, reverent and respectful toward the true Dhamma; subduing the negligence of others, always abounding in spiritual urgency.

1033.

1033.

Vodātacittasaṅkappo[V 0.0094], pāpicchāmalavajjito;

Micchādiṭṭhimatikkanto, saddhammesu patiṭṭhito.

Pure in thought and intention, free from the stain of evil desires; having transcended wrong views, established in the true Dhamma.

1034.

1034.

Cetokhilasamucchedī, vinibandhaviveṭhako;

Mānasaṃ sampahaṃseti, saṃkilesavimuttiyā.

Cutting off mental barrenness, unraveling the bonds; he makes the mind glad by freedom from defilements.

1035.

1035.

Pavivitto asaṃsaṭṭho, santo appicchatārato;

Ariyāvaṃsālaṅkāro, supposo subharo sukhī.

Secluded, unentangled, peaceful, delighting in fewness of wishes; adorned with the lineage of the Noble Ones, easy to support, easy to maintain, happy.

1036.

1036.

Sallekhavutti dhutavā, pāpāpacayatapparo;

Pāsādikasamācāro, pasādabahulo muni.

Practicing effacement, observing the ascetic practices, intent on the removal of evil; the sage of pleasing conduct abounds in serenity.

1037.

1037.

Anuddhato acapalo,

Danto gutto yatindriyo;

Cetosamādhigaruko,

Sampajāno satīyuto.

Not haughty, not fickle, tamed, guarded, with senses controlled; respectful of mental concentration, clearly comprehending and mindful.

1038.

1038.

Ussāhajāto saddhamme, chandajāto nirantaraṃ;

Sātaccakārī svākāro, paṭipattiparāyaṇo.

Energetic in the true Dhamma, with zeal constantly arisen; persevering in action, of good demeanor, devoted to the practice.

1039.

1039.

Cetokāḷakāpagato, bhāvanārasamuttamaṃ;

Raṅgaṃ niddhotavatthaṃva, sādhukaṃ paṭigaṇhati.

Freed from mental stain, he readily accepts the supreme flavor of meditation, like a cloth cleansed of dye.

1040.

1040.

Iti sampāditākāro, parisuddhamanoratho;

Nirādīnavasañcāro, sotthipatto niraṅgaṇo.

Thus perfected in conduct, pure in aspiration; wandering free from danger, having attained well-being, without defilement.

1041.

1041.

Pāpagāhavinimutto, rāhumuttova candimā;

Guṇaraṃsiparikkhitto, sobheti jinasāsanaṃ.

Freed from the grip of evil, like the moon released from Rāhu; encompassed by rays of virtue, he beautifies the Conqueror’s Dispensation.

1042.

1042.

Iccālobhamadosañca, mohābhāvamathāparaṃ;

Nekkhammaṃ pavivekañca, tathā nissaraṇaṃ budho.

Thus the wise one understands non-greed and non-hatred, and further, the absence of delusion, renunciation and seclusion, and likewise, liberation.

1043.

1043.

Samārabbha [M 0.0089] visodhento, ajjhāsayamasesato;

Dhīro sampaṭipādeti, bhāvanāsukhamuttamaṃ.

Striving and purifying his disposition completely, the wise one brings about the supreme bliss of cultivation.

1044.

1044.

Tato [V 0.0095] paṇītādhimutti, palibodhavinissaṭo;

Paripanthavinimutto, vigatāvaraṇālayo.

Then, with sublime resolution, freed from impediments, released from obstructions, with hindrances and attachments gone.

1045.

1045.

Bhāvanāninnasantāno, kallacitto visārado;

Kasiṇādikamārabbha, bhāveyya samathaṃ kathaṃ.

With a mind-stream inclined to meditation, with a sound mind, skilled; having undertaken the kasiṇas and so forth, how should one develop serenity?

1046.

1046.

Pathavīkasiṇaṃ tāva, vidatthicaturaṅgulaṃ;

Katvānāruṇavaṇṇāya, mattikāya sumaṇḍalaṃ.

First, as to the earth kasiṇa: having made a fine circular disk of dawn-colored clay, a span and four fingers in diameter.

1047.

1047.

Yugamatte ṭhapetvāna, ṭhāne sukhanisinnako;

Pathavīti samaññāya, katvābhogaṃ tu bhāvaye.

Having placed it at a yoke's distance, while seated comfortably in a suitable place, one should develop it, giving attention to the concept, 'earth'.

1048.

1048.

Akatepi khalādimhi, akiccheneva maṇḍale;

Nimittaṃ jāyaticcāhu, pubbayogavato pana.

But for one with previous practice, they say the sign arises effortlessly, even on a disk not prepared on a threshing floor or the like.

1049.

1049.

Āpomaṇḍalamuggaṇhe, bhājanādigate jale;

Tejamhi tejokasiṇaṃ, paṭacchiddādisaṃgate.

One should apprehend the water-disk in water contained in a vessel or the like; and the fire-kasiṇa in fire associated with a hole in a screen or the like.

1050.

1050.

Sassaggādimhi kammante, vāyokasiṇamaṇḍalaṃ;

Paṭibhāgasamācāro, phuṭṭhaṭṭhāneva jāyati.

For the wind-kasiṇa, in the practice involving the tips of grain and so on, the counterpart sign arises as if in the very place that was touched.

1051.

1051.

Nīlādikasiṇaṃ vatthe, pupphe vā vaṇṇadhātuyaṃ;

Ākāsamaṇḍalaṃ bhitti-chiddādimhi upaṭṭhitaṃ.

The blue and other kasiṇas are prepared on cloth, a flower, or a colored element; the space-kasiṇa is established in a wall-opening or the like.

1052.

1052.

Chiddappaviṭṭhamālokaṃ, uggaṇheyya patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Sūriyālokādibhedaṃ, bhūmiyaṃ vātha bhittiyaṃ.

One should apprehend the light that has entered through an opening and is established, whether on the ground or on a wall, this light being of various kinds, such as sunlight.

1053.

1053.

Dasadhā kasiṇesvevaṃ, yattha katthaci yogino;

Parikammaṃ karontassa, uggaho nāma jāyati.

Thus, for a yogī performing the preliminary work on the ten kasiṇas in any location whatsoever, what is known as the learning sign arises.

1054.

1054.

Cittassupaṭṭhite tasmiṃ, passantasseva cakkhunā;

Uggahamhi nimittamhi, paṭipādeyya bhāvanaṃ.

When that learning sign is well-established in the mind, for one seeing it as if with the physical eye, one should undertake the cultivation upon it.

1055.

1055.

Vikkhepaṃ vinivārento, paripanthe virājayaṃ;

Nimittābhimukheneva, mānasaṃ paṭipādaye.

Warding off distraction, becoming dispassionate towards obstacles, one should direct the mind straight towards the sign.

1056.

1056.

Āsevantassa [M 0.0090][V 0.0096] tassevaṃ, cittaṃ hoti samāhitaṃ;

Saṃklesā sannisīdanti, paṭibhāgo ca jāyati.

For one thus cultivating, the mind becomes concentrated; defilements subside, and the counterpart sign arises.

1057.

1057.

Tattha paṇṇattisaṅkhāte, nimitte bhāvanāmaye;

Tatheva paṭibhāgamhi, tato yuñjeyya bhāvanaṃ.

Therein, upon that sign produced by cultivation and designated as a concept, and likewise upon the counterpart sign, one should then apply oneself to meditation.

1058.

1058.

Tatthādhimutto satimā, nimittavidhikovido;

Indriyāni samānento, sappāyamupalakkhayaṃ.

Therein, resolute and mindful, skilled in the method concerning the sign, balancing the faculties, and discerning what is suitable,

1059.

1059.

Niggayha uddhataṃ cittaṃ, paggayha līnamānasaṃ;

Ūhataṃ sampahaṃsento, upekkhanto samāhitaṃ.

Restraining the agitated mind, uplifting the sluggish mind, gladdening the troubled mind, and regarding the concentrated mind with equanimity.

1060.

1060.

Reṇumhi uppaladale, sutte nāvāya nāḷiyā;

Yathā madhukarādīnaṃ, pavatti samma vaṇṇitā.

As dust on a lotus leaf, or a boat in a trough, or as the activity of bees and so forth, so is its behavior well described.

1061.

1061.

Cittapavattiākāraṃ, sādhukaṃ lakkhayaṃ budho;

Tathā samenākārena, pahitatto parakkame.

The wise one, carefully discerning the mode of the mind's activity, should then strive with a resolute mind and in an even manner.

1062.

1062.

Samappavattamākāraṃ, sallakkhetvā nirantaraṃ;

Padahantassa tassevaṃ, appanā nāma jāyati.

Having continuously discerned the manner of its even flow, for one thus striving, what is known as absorption arises.

1063.

1063.

Paṭibhāganimittaṃ tu, vaḍḍheyya kasiṇaṃ puna;

Upacārabhūmiyaṃ vā, appanāyaṃ va katthaci.

One should further expand the counterpart sign, the kasiṇa, either in the access stage, in absorption, or anywhere.

1064.

1064.

Ekaṅguladvaṅgulādi-vaseneva yathākkamaṃ;

Pharanto manasāyeva, nipuṇo yāvadicchakaṃ.

A skillful one, spreading it with the mind itself, does so by means of one finger, two fingers, and so on, in due order, as far as one wishes.

1065.

1065.

Tatthevaṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ, patvāna paguṇaṃ tato;

Katvā ciṇṇavasībhūtā, tamhā vuṭṭhāya paṇḍito.

The wise one, having thus attained the first jhāna there, and then having made it proficient, practiced, and mastered, rising from it...

1066.

1066.

Vitakkādikathūlaṅgaṃ, pahānāya yathākkamaṃ;

Tatheva paṭipajjanto, pappoti dutiyādayo.

For abandoning the coarse factors beginning with initial application, in due order, proceeding in the same way, one attains the second jhāna and so forth.

1067.

1067.

Dasadhā kasiṇānevaṃ, bhāvetvā pana yogino;

Catukkapañcakajjhānaṃ, katvā vikkhepanissaṭā.

Yogis, having thus developed the ten kasiṇas, having attained the fourfold and fivefold jhānas, and being free from distraction...

1068.

1068.

Supakkhālitupaklesā[V 0.0097], santacittā samāhitā;

Pavivekarasassādaṃ, anubhonti yathāsukhaṃ.

With defilements well-washed away, their minds peaceful and concentrated, they experience the taste of seclusion as they please.

1069.

1069.

Asubhaṃ [M 0.0091] pana bhāvento, nimittaṃ yattha katthaci;

Uddhumātādibhedamhi, uggaṇheyyāsubhe kathaṃ?

But when developing the meditation on foulness, how should one apprehend the foul sign among the types beginning with the bloated, wherever it may be?

1070.

1070.

Ekāhādimatikkantaṃ, uddhumātakamīritaṃ;

Vigatacchavi bībhacchaṃ, nīlākāraṃ vinīlakaṃ.

That which has passed one day or more is called the bloated; that which is skinless, repulsive, and blue in appearance is the discolored.

1071.

1071.

Vikiṇṇapubbakudhitaṃ, paribhinnaṃ vipubbakaṃ;

Viccheditaṅgapaccaṅgaṃ, vicchiddakaṃ kaḷevaraṃ.

That which is putrid with oozing pus and burst open is the festering corpse; the body with its limbs and members severed is the cut-up corpse.

1072.

1072.

Vividhākārapāṇehi, khajjamānaṃ vikhāditaṃ;

Vināsitaṅgapaccaṅgaṃ, vikkhittanti pavuccati.

Being devoured and gnawed by creatures of various kinds, with limbs and minor limbs destroyed—this is called the scattered corpse.

1073.

1073.

Pādādibhaṅgavikkhittaṃ, hatavikkhittakaṃ mataṃ;

Lohitaṃ lohitākiṇṇaṃ, puḷavaṃ kimisaṅkulaṃ.

Scattered with broken feet and so on is the scattered corpse; known as such is the hacked-and-scattered. The bloody is covered with blood; the worm-infested is teeming with worms.

1074.

1074.

Aṭṭhisaṅkhalikāmattaṃ, aṭṭhikanti ca sabbathā;

Saṇṭhānākārabhedena, dasadhāsubhadesanā.

Merely a chain of bones, in every way, is the skeleton. Through such distinctions of form and appearance, the teaching of the ten kinds of foulness is given.

1075.

1075.

Tatthevaṃ dasadhā bhede, nijjīvakuṇapāsubhe;

Ujjhite bhūmibhāgasmiṃ, matakāye kaḷevare.

Thus, with regard to these ten types: the lifeless, foul corpse, the dead body, the carcass, discarded on a piece of ground...

1076.

1076.

Labbhamānakamākāraṃ, oloketvā salakkhaṇaṃ;

Uggahetvāna cittena, taṃtaṃnāmena bhāvaye.

Observing the appearance that is found, together with its characteristics, and having apprehended it with the mind, one should develop it by its respective name.

1077.

1077.

Paṭikūlañca jegucchaṃ, duggandhañca virūpakaṃ;

Harāyitamajaññañca, hīḷitaṃ vikkhitāsivaṃ.

Repulsive and disgusting, foul-smelling and deformed; shameful and ignoble, despised, scattered, and wretched.

1078.

1078.

Iccevamasubhākāre,

Katvābhogaṃ tu yogino;

Bhāventassupacāro ca,

Paṭibhāgo ca jāyati.

Thus, for the yogi who gives attention to these foul aspects and develops the meditation, access concentration and the counterpart sign arise.

1079.

1079.

Paṭibhāganimittaṃ [V 0.0098] tu, upacārena sevato;

Appeti paṭhamajjhāna-metthevaṃ samathe nayo.

But for one who cultivates the counterpart sign by means of access concentration, the first jhāna is attained. Such is the method in serenity meditation.

1080.

1080.

Vinā [M 0.0092] saddhammaṃ panidaṃ, sarīraṃ bālananditaṃ;

Vipattipariyosānaṃ, avassaṃ bhedagāmikaṃ.

But without the true Dhamma, this body, delighted in by fools, has ruin as its end, inevitably tending to dissolution.

1081.

1081.

Yathā idaṃ tathā etaṃ, yathā etaṃ tathā idaṃ;

Jīvamānañca nijjīvameva dhammaparāyaṇaṃ.

As this is, so is that; as that is, so is this. Both the living and the lifeless are indeed subject to the law of nature.

1082.

1082.

Sabhāvo sopi dehassa,

Sabbassāpi ca sabbathā;

Vicitabbā dhirenāpi,

Esāyaṃ niyatā gati.

Such is the nature of this body, and of all things in every way. This should be investigated even by the wise, for this is the fixed destiny.

1083.

1083.

Aniccaṃ khayadhammañca, dukkhameva bhayāvahaṃ;

Anattā ca parābhūtā, vibbhijjati khaṇe khaṇe.

Impermanent and subject to decay, suffering itself and bringing fear; not-self and overcome, it breaks up moment by moment.

1084.

1084.

Vināsamānassākāraṃ, tatthevaṃ pana passato;

Vipassanābhāvanāti, tamīrenti tathāgatā.

But for one who thus sees the manner of its destruction, that the Tathāgatas declare to be the development of insight.

1085.

1085.

Bhāvanaṃ duvidhampetaṃ, bhāventi puna paṇḍitā;

Jīvamānepi kāyamhi, taṃtadākārasambhave.

The wise again cultivate these two kinds of meditation even in the living body, when those respective appearances arise.

1086.

1086.

Jīvamānopi kāyoyaṃ,

Kuṇapova sabhāvato;

Tamalaṅkārapaṭicchanno,

Bālānaṃ na pakāsati.

Even while alive, this body is by nature like a corpse; covered by adornments, it is not apparent to fools.

1087.

1087.

Bahi maṭṭhamupaṭṭhāti, anto kuṇapapūritaṃ;

Uggharantaṃ paggharantaṃ, navadvāramalassavaṃ.

Outwardly it appears polished, but inwardly it is filled with foulness; oozing and dripping, with impurities flowing from its nine doors.

1088.

1088.

Sarīraṃ niccaduggandhaṃ, nānākimisamākulaṃ;

Tacamaṃsapaṭicchannaṃ, aṭṭhipañjarasaṇṭhitaṃ.

The body is constantly foul-smelling, teeming with various worms, covered with skin and flesh, and established upon a cage of bones.

1089.

1089.

Vaccakūpamidaṃ [V 0.0099] nāma, dvattiṃsāsucipūritaṃ;

Narānukkārabhūmīva, nekavassagaṇocitā.

This is called a cesspool, filled with the thirty-two impurities; like a charnel ground piled high over many years.

1090.

1090.

Susānagamanosānaṃ, bahusādhāraṇāsubhaṃ;

Gaṇḍabhūtaṃ sallabhūtaṃ, bahudukkhanibandhanaṃ.

Destined for the charnel ground, a foul thing common to many; it has become a boil, it has become a dart, a cause for much suffering.

1091.

1091.

Nānābyādhisamākiṇṇaṃ[M 0.0093], nānopaddavasaṃkulaṃ;

Nānānatthasamodhānaṃ, nānāsaṃklesavatthukaṃ.

Afflicted with various diseases, beset by various calamities, a collection of various misfortunes, a basis for various defilements.

1092.

1092.

Positampi ciraṃ kālaṃ, mamaṃkāramamāyitaṃ;

Lahudujjanamittova, pīḷitaṃ sampadussati.

Though nourished for a long time and treated as 'mine', when afflicted it becomes utterly corrupt, like an unreliable and wicked friend.

1093.

1093.

Parihāyati nissāraṃ, jaratāpi taṃ yobbanaṃ;

Maccubhajjitamaccanta-masesaṃ paribhijjati.

It declines, being essenceless; youth, too, is worn away by old age. Relentlessly crushed by death, it utterly breaks apart without remainder.

1094.

1094.

Tathāpi jālasantāno, bahusambhārasaṅkhato;

Vatthālaṅkārasañchanno, mālāgandhādisobhito.

Yet even so, this network of flesh, assembled from many constituents, covered with robes and ornaments, beautified with garlands, perfumes, and so forth—

1095.

1095.

Saviññattivikārehi, vicittākāramaṇḍito;

Kāyo līḷavilāsehi, palambheti mahājanaṃ.

Adorned with diverse appearances, with expressive gestures and transformations, the body, with its captivating charms, allures the multitude.

1096.

1096.

Vañcitā yena dummedhā, kāmaklesamalīmayā;

Pūrenti caturāpāyaṃ, māradheyyānusārino.

Fooled by it are the unwise, stained with the filth of sensual defilements; following Māra’s dominion, they fill the four states of misery.

1097.

1097.

Evamādīnavaṃ ñatvā, pūtikāye vicakkhaṇā;

Asubhādikamākāra-mārabbha chandupaṭṭhahuṃ.

Having thus known the danger in this putrid body, the discerning, undertaking the perception of repulsiveness and so on, arouse the will.

1098.

1098.

Yasmiṃ patanti kuṇape viparītasaññā,

Saṃklesapāpavasagā visamaṃ carantā;

Taṃ passathetamasubhampi vināsadhammaṃ,

Iccevamāha sugato dasadhā vibhāgaṃ.

Those with distorted perceptions, under the sway of defilements and evil, behaving wrongly, become attached to this corpse. See that this repulsive thing is itself subject to destruction! Thus the Well-Gone-One spoke of the ten-fold division.

1099.

1099.

Satthārā kasiṇañca yaṃ dasavidhaṃ vikkhepavikkhambhanaṃ,

Kāmaklesavināsanaṃ dasavidhaṃ yañcāsubhaṃ bhāsitaṃ;

Dibbabrahmasukhāvahaṃ [V 0.0100] samapadaṃ vijjodayaṃ yoginā,

Kammaṭṭhānamalaṃ tamuttamaguṇenāsevitaṃ sevituṃ.

The Teacher has declared the ten-fold kasina for suppressing distractions, and the ten-fold repulsiveness for destroying sensual defilements; that pure meditation subject—which brings divine and Brahma-like happiness, leads to a state of calm, and gives rise to knowledge for the yogi—should be cultivated, as it is practiced by those of supreme virtue.

Iti nāmarūpaparicchede kasiṇāsubhavibhāgo nāma

Thus ends the section on Kasina and the Repulsive in the Discrimination of Name and Form.

Aṭṭhamo paricchedo.

The Eighth Chapter.

9. Navamo paricchedo

9. The Ninth Chapter

Dasānussativibhāgo

The Exposition of the Ten Recollections.

1100.

1100.

Saddhāpabbajito [M 0.0094] yogī, bhāventonussatiṃ pana;

Dasānussatibhedesu, bhāveyyaññataraṃ kathaṃ.

How should a yogi who has gone forth in faith, while developing recollection, develop one or another among the ten kinds of recollection?

1101.

1101.

Arahaṃ sugato loke, bhagavā lokapāragū;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, vimuttiparināyako.

The Arahant, the Well-Gone-One in the world, the Blessed One, who has gone beyond the world; perfect in knowledge and conduct, the leader to liberation.

1102.

1102.

Jeṭṭho sammābhisambuddho, seṭṭho purisasārathī;

Satthā devamanussānaṃ, buddho appaṭipuggalo.

The foremost, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the supreme charioteer of men; the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, without peer.

1103.

1103.

Sabbalokahito bandhu, samattaratanālayo;

Sattānamanukampāya, jāto nātho sivaṃkaro.

The benefactor of all worlds, a kinsman, the abode of all the jewels; out of compassion for beings, the protector, the maker of peace, was born.

1104.

1104.

Cakkhumā titthakusalo, dhammassāmī tathāgato;

Maccudheyyavimokkhāya, paṭipādayi pāṇino.

The Visionary, skilled in doctrines, the Tathāgata, Lord of the Dhamma, leads beings to release from the realm of Death.

1105.

1105.

Satthavāho mahāyoggo, maggāmaggayudhandharo;

Sirisatthamadhiggayha, vicarittha mahāpathaṃ,

The caravan leader, a great yogi, who knows the path and the non-path; having attained the glorious goal, he wandered the great road.

1106.

1106.

Anomo asamo dhīro,

Lokahītaparakkamo;

Sabbākāravaropeto[V 0.0101],

Accherabbhutapuggalo.

Noble, unequalled, wise, striving for the world's benefit; endowed with all excellent qualities, a wonderful and amazing person.

1107.

1107.

Atthabhūto dhammabhūto,

Brahmabhūto mahāyaso;

Ñāṇālokaparicchinna-

Ñeyyāsesapariggaho.

Become the goal, become the Dhamma, become Brahmā, of great glory; comprehending all that can be known, which is defined by the light of knowledge.

1108.

1108.

Ānubhāvavasippatto, āsabhaṇḍānaniccalo;

Mahantamariyādoyamanantagatigocaro.

Attained to the mastery of power, pre-eminent and unshakable; of vast domain, of boundless range.

1109.

1109.

Sabbā bhiññābalappatto, vesārajjavisārado;

Sabbasampattiniṭṭhāno, guṇapāramipūrako.

Possessed of all higher knowledges and powers, skilled in self-confidence; the culmination of all accomplishments, the fulfiller of the perfections of virtue.

1110.

1110.

Appameyyo [M 0.0095] mahānāgo, mahāvīro mahāmuni;

Mahesī mahitācāro, mahāmaho mahiddhiko.

Immeasurable, great nāga, great hero, great silent sage; great seer, of esteemed conduct, of great splendor, of great power.

1111.

1111.

Sabbatthasiddhisañcāro, mahesīgaṇapūjito;

Rājādhirājamahito, devabrahmābhivandito.

Everywhere he moves with success, honored by the hosts of great sages; revered by the king of kings, worshipped by devas and Brahmās.

1112.

1112.

Abhibhūya tayo loke, ādiccova nabhantare;

Virocati mahātejo, andhakāre pabhaṅkaro.

Having overcome the three worlds, like the sun in the sky, he shines with great splendor, the dispeller of darkness.

1113.

1113.

Byāmappabhāparikkhitto, ketumālāhalaṅkato;

Dvattiṃsalakkhaṇāsītianubyañjanasobhito.

Surrounded by a fathom's radiance, adorned with a garland of rays; beautiful with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics.

1114.

1114.

Chabbaṇṇaraṃsilalito, ratanagghiyasannibho;

Samiddhirūpasobhaggo, dassaneyyaṃva piṇḍitaṃ.

Charming with six-colored rays, like a heap of precious gems; possessed of flourishing beauty, as if loveliness incarnate.

1115.

1115.

Phullaṃ padumasaṇḍaṃva, kapparukkhovalaṅkato;

Nabhaṃva tārakākiṇṇaṃ, uttamo paṭidissati.

Like a lotus grove in full bloom, or like an adorned wish-fulfilling tree; like the star-filled sky, the Supreme One appears.

1116.

1116.

Satthukappamahāvīraputtehi parivārito;

Sabbalokamahiddhāya, dhammarājā sayaṃvasī.

Surrounded by heroic disciples worthy of the Teacher, of great power for all the world; the King of Dhamma, self-mastered.

1117.

1117.

Niddhotamalacandova[V 0.0102], nakkhattaparivārito;

Khattasaṅghaparibyuḷho, cakkavattīva sobhati.

Like the moon freed from stains, surrounded by stars; amidst the assembly of nobles, he shines like a universal monarch.

1118.

1118.

Iccānantaguṇākiṇṇamasesamalanissaṭaṃ;

Sabbasampattidātāraṃ, vipattivinibandhakaṃ.

Thus, replete with infinite virtues, free from all defilements; the giver of all attainments, the severer of misfortune's bonds.

1119.

1119.

Dayāparamahorattaṃ, bhagavantamanussaraṃ;

Bhāveti paññavā yogī, buddhānussatibhāvanaṃ.

The wise yogi, full of compassion, recollecting the Blessed One day and night, cultivates the development of the recollection of the Buddha.

1120.

1120.

Svākhāto tena saddhammo, sambuddhena satīmatā;

Paccattapaṭivedhena, passitabbo yathārahaṃ.

Well-proclaimed is the True Dhamma by him, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the mindful one; it is to be seen through personal realization, as is fitting.

1121.

1121.

Taṇhādaliddanāsāya, manorathasamiddhiyā;

Kālantaramanāgamma, paccakkhaphaladāyako.

For the destruction of the poverty of craving, for the fulfillment of aspirations; without delay, it is the giver of immediate fruit.

1122.

1122.

Upanissayavantānaṃ, “ehi passā”ti dassiyo;

Paccattameva viññūhi, veditabbo sabhāvato.

For those with supporting conditions, it is to be shown as 'Come and see'; it is to be understood individually by the wise, according to its own nature.

1123.

1123.

Sabbāsavasamugghātī[M 0.0096], suddho sovatthiko sivo;

Pihitāpāyakummaggo, maggo nibbānapattiyā.

Uprooter of all taints, pure, conducive to well-being, auspicious; blocking the wrong path to the states of misery, it is the path for the attainment of Nibbāna.

1124.

1124.

Klesasaṃkaṭaduggamhā, dukkhakkhandhamahabbhayā;

Khemantabhūmiṃ niyyāti, accantamanupaddavaṃ.

From the perilous, difficult path of defilements, from the mass of suffering and from great fear, it leads to the land of safety, utterly free from affliction.

1125.

1125.

Puññatitthamidaṃ nāma, maṅgalañca sivaṅkaraṃ;

Hitodayasukhādhāna-mamatāhāramuttamaṃ.

This is called the ford of merit, auspicious and bringing welfare; the foundation for the arising of benefit and happiness, the supreme remover of attachment.

1126.

1126.

Avijjāpaṭaluddhāravijjānettosadhaṃ varaṃ;

Paññādhāramidaṃ satthaṃ, klesagaṇḍappabhedakaṃ.

An excellent medicine that is the eye of true knowledge, removing the cataract of ignorance; this teaching is a vessel of wisdom, a breaker of the boil of defilements.

1127.

1127.

Caturoghanimuggānaṃ, setubandho samuggato;

Bhavacārakaruddhānaṃ, mahādvāro apāruto.

For those immersed in the four floods, a causeway has arisen; for those confined in the prison of existence, a great door has been opened.

1128.

1128.

Sokopāyāsaviddhānaṃ, paridevasamaṅginaṃ;

Sallanīharaṇopāyo, accantasukhamīrito.

For those pierced by sorrow and despair, who are full of lamentation, the means for extracting the dart is proclaimed as ultimate happiness.

1129.

1129.

Byasanopaddavāpeto[V 0.0103], saṃklesamalanissaṭo;

Ujusammattaniyato, paṭipattivisuddhiyā.

Free from calamity and misfortune, escaped from the stain of defilements, it is fixed on the straight path of rightness through purity of practice.

1130.

1130.

Suddhasīlaparikkhāro, samādhimayapañjaro;

Sammāsaṅkappacakkaṅgo, sammāvāyāmavāhano.

With pure virtue as its equipment, with concentration as its framework, with right thought as its wheel-component, with right effort as its draught-animal.

1131.

1131.

Satisārathisaṃyutto, sammādiṭṭhipurejavo;

Esa dhammaratho yāti, yogakkhemassa pattiyā.

Endowed with mindfulness as its charioteer, with right view as its forerunner, this Dhamma-chariot proceeds for the attainment of security from bondage.

1132.

1132.

Vipattipaṭibāhāya, sabbasampattisiddhiyā;

Sabbakhandhavimokkhāya, dhammaṃ desesi cakkhumā.

For warding off misfortune, for achieving all success, for liberation from all aggregates, the One with Vision taught the Dhamma.

1133.

1133.

Hitesī sabbapāṇīnaṃ, dayāpanno mahāmuni;

Dhammālokaṃ pakāsesi, cakkhumantānamuttamo.

Seeking the welfare of all beings, the Great Sage, full of compassion, the foremost among those with vision, illuminated the light of the Dhamma.

1134.

1134.

Yaṃ dhammaṃ sammadaññāya, khemamaggappatiṭṭhitā;

Pāpakāpagatā dhīrā, passaddhidarathāsayā.

Having rightly understood that Dhamma, established on the path of security, the wise, departed from evil, have their agitated dispositions calmed.

1135.

1135.

Bhavayogā vinimuttā, pahīnabhayabheravā;

Accantasukhamedhenti, sotthipattā mahesayo.

The great sages, freed from the bonds of becoming, having abandoned fear and dread, having attained well-being, reach ultimate happiness.

1136.

1136.

Tamevamuttamaṃ [M 0.0097] dhammaṃ, cintento pana paṇḍito;

Bhāvetīti pakāsenti, dhammānussatibhāvanaṃ.

Thus reflecting on that supreme Dhamma, the wise one develops the meditation on the recollection of the Dhamma; so they declare.

1137.

1137.

Cattāro ca paṭipannā, cattāro ca phale ṭhitā;

Esa saṅgho ujubhūto, paññāsīlasamāhito.

Four are those practicing the way, and four are established in the fruit; this is the Sangha that is upright, composed in wisdom and virtue.

1138.

1138.

Palāpāpagato suddho, paṭipattipatiṭṭhito;

Pariggahitasaddhammo, samiddhiguṇasobhito.

Pure, having gone beyond prattle, established in the practice, having fully grasped the True Dhamma, resplendent with successful virtues.

1139.

1139.

Pahīnāpāyagamano, pāpaklesavinissaṭo;

Paripanthasamucchedī, bhavacārakabhedako.

Having abandoned the way to the states of woe, escaped from evil defilements, an exterminator of obstacles, a breaker of the prison of existence.

1140.

1140.

Uttamadamathappatto, suvinīto mahesinā;

Vijjāvimuttivodāto, ājānīyapathe ṭhito.

Having attained supreme self-control, well-disciplined by the Great Sage, purified by knowledge and liberation, standing on the path of the thoroughbred.

1141.

1141.

Sugatorasi [V 0.0104] sambhūto, sucidhammasirindharo;

Paṭipāditasampatto, dhammasāsanasevito.

Born from the chest of the Well-Gone One, bearing the glorious crown of the pure Dhamma, having achieved the accomplishment, devoted to the Dispensation of the Dhamma.

1142.

1142.

Bhayabheravanissaṅgo, jinatejānupālito;

Moneyyapathasañcāro, sugatovādabhājano.

Without clinging to fear and terror, protected by the Victor's majesty, journeying on the path of sagehood, a vessel for the Well-Gone One's instruction.

1143.

1143.

Appamādaparittāṇo, sīlālaṅkārabhūsito;

Cetosamādhisannaddho, paññāyudhasamujjalo.

Having diligence as their protection, adorned with the ornament of virtue, armored with concentration of mind, resplendent with the weapon of wisdom.

1144.

1144.

Ujumaggamadhiṭṭhāya, mārakāyappadālano;

Aparājitasaṅgāmo, lalitodātavikkamo.

Established on the straight path, a shatterer of Māra's host, unvanquished in battle, of graceful and pure valor.

1145.

1145.

Maccudheyyamatikkanto, bodhidhammappatiṭṭhito;

Chaḷābhiññābalappatto, samārādhitasāsano.

Having transcended the domain of Death, established in the Dhamma of Awakening, having attained the power of the six super-knowledges, one who has fulfilled the Teaching.

1146.

1146.

Anubodhimanuppatto, pabhinnapaṭisambhido;

Sāmaññapāramippatto, toseti jinamānasaṃ.

Having attained realization, with the analytical knowledges mastered, having reached the perfection of the ascetic's life, he pleases the mind of the Conqueror.

1147.

1147.

Nekākāravarūpeto, nānāsampattiphullito;

Vipattipathanittiṇṇo, abhibuddhiparāyaṇo.

Endowed with many excellent qualities, blossoming with various accomplishments, having crossed over the path of misfortune, with supreme awakening as the final goal.

1148.

1148.

Āhuneyyo [M 0.0098] pāhuneyyo,

Dakkhiṇeyyo sudullabho;

Sadevakassa lokassa,

Puññakkhettamanuttaraṃ.

Worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, very rare; for the world together with its deities, an unsurpassed field of merit.

1149.

1149.

Yattha suddhimhi niddose, saddhābījaṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Accantaṃ paripāceti, sampattiphalamuttamaṃ.

Where, in stainless purity, the seed of faith is established, it thoroughly ripens into the supreme fruit of attainment.

1150.

1150.

Yaṃ phalaṃ paribhuñjantā, vimuttirasasevanaṃ;

Accantasukhitā dhīrā, bhavanti ajarāmarā.

Enjoying that fruit, partaking of the taste of liberation, the wise become utterly happy, ageless and deathless.

1151.

1151.

Taṃ phalaṃ patthayantena, saṅghānussatibhāvanā;

Bhāvetabbā paniccevamiti bhāsanti paṇḍitā.

For one aspiring to that fruit, the development of the recollection of the Sangha should be cultivated; thus the wise declare.

1152.

1152.

Pañcasīlaṃ [V 0.0105] dasasīlaṃ, pātimokkhamuposathaṃ;

Cātupārisuddhisīlaṃ, dhutaṅgaparivāritaṃ.

The five precepts, the ten precepts, the Pātimokkha and the Uposatha, the fourfold purity of virtue, surrounded by the ascetic practices.

1153.

1153.

Evametesu yaṃ kiñci, samādāya rahogato;

Tamānisaṃsaṃ guṇato, phalato ca vicintaye.

Whatever one undertakes among these, having gone into solitude, one should contemplate its benefits in terms of qualities and results.

1154.

1154.

Ādi cetaṃ patiṭṭhā ca, mukhaṃ pamukhamuttamaṃ;

Mūlaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ, pabhavaṃ paṭipattiyā.

It is the beginning and the foundation, the entrance, the foremost, the supreme; the root of wholesome qualities, the origin of practice.

1155.

1155.

Sāsanotaraṇadvāraṃ, titthaṃ saddhammavāpiyā;

Pārisuddhipadaṭṭhānaṃ, maggo khemantapāpako.

The door to crossing over the Dispensation, the ford of the true Dhamma's pond, the basis for purity, the path leading to security.

1156.

1156.

Sādhu sikkhāsamādānaṃ, bāhusaccavibhūsanaṃ;

Ariyācāracāritta-mavaṇṇamalavajjanaṃ.

Good is the undertaking of training, an adornment of vast learning, the conduct and practice of the noble ones, avoiding blame and stain.

1157.

1157.

Kulaputtaalaṅkāro, pāpajallapavāhanaṃ;

Anapāyi sugandhañca, mahāpurisasevitaṃ.

The ornament of a clansman, washing away the dirt of evil, an unfailing fragrance, resorted to by great persons.

1158.

1158.

Pacchānutāpaharaṇaṃ, pītipāmojjavaḍḍhanaṃ;

Nekkhammabhāvanopetaṃ, pabbajjāvesasobhanaṃ.

It removes later regret, increases joy and gladness, is endowed with the development of renunciation, and beautifies the appearance of one gone forth.

1159.

1159.

Sopānaṃ saggalokassa, daḷhāpāyavidhānakaṃ;

Anupaddavasampatti, samatthaguṇasūdanī.

A stairway to the heavenly world, providing a firm defense against states of woe, success without misfortune, destroying all unwholesome qualities.

1160.

1160.

Klesapañjaravicchedi[M 0.0099], vipattipathavāraṇaṃ;

Sotthikammasamuṭṭhānaṃ, asādhāraṇamaṅgalaṃ.

It cuts through the cage of defilements, wards off the path of misfortune, is the origin of safe conduct, an incomparable blessing.

1161.

1161.

“Suladdhā vata me laddhā, saddhā sugatasāsane;

Sīlaṃ me yassa kalyāṇaṃ, parisuddhamakhaṇḍitaṃ.

“Truly well-gained is my gain, faith in the Sugata’s Dispensation; my virtue is auspicious, perfectly pure and unbroken.”

1162.

1162.

“Dullabho vata me laddho,

Mahālābho anappako;

Yohamakkhalitācāro,

Upaghātavivajjito.

“Truly rare is what I have gained, a great and not insignificant gain—I whose conduct is unblemished, free from harm.”

1163.

1163.

“Dhammaṅkuritasantāno[V 0.0106], mūlajātosmi sāsane;

Ujumaggaṃ samāruḷho, pihitā sabhayā disā.

“With a continuity sprouted from the Dhamma, I am rooted in the Dispensation; having ascended the straight path, all fearful directions are closed off.”

1164.

1164.

“Avañcā vata me jāti, āraddhā khaṇasampadā;

Patiṭṭhitomhi saddhamme, saphalaṃ mama jīvitaṃ”.

“Truly, my birth is not in vain, the opportune moment has been seized; I am established in the true Dhamma, my life is fruitful.”

1165.

1165.

Itthaṃ nānappakārena, cintento guṇamattano;

Sīlakkhandhassa bhāveti, sīlānussatibhāvanaṃ.

Thus, reflecting in various ways on the virtues of one's own aggregate of virtue, one cultivates the development of the recollection of virtue.

1166.

1166.

Saddhāya sīlavantesu, datvā dānaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Niddhotamalamacchero, vivitto tamanussare.

Having given gifts with faith and appropriately to the virtuous, with the stain of avarice washed clean, secluded, one should recollect that.

1167.

1167.

Dānaṃ nidhānamanugaṃ, asādhāraṇamuttamaṃ;

Avināsasukhādhānaṃ, accantaṃ sabbakāmadaṃ.

Giving is a treasure that follows after, supreme and incomparable, a store of imperishable happiness, completely fulfilling all desires.

1168.

1168.

Kopadāhopasamanaṃ, maccheramalasodhanaṃ;

Pamādaniddāvuṭṭhānaṃ, lobhapāsavimocanaṃ.

It calms the fever of anger, cleanses the stain of stinginess, is an awakening from the sleep of negligence, a release from the snare of greed.

1169.

1169.

Cetovikāradamanaṃ, micchāmagganivāraṇaṃ;

Vittilābhasukhassādo, vibhavodayamaṅgalaṃ.

It tames the mind's distortions, averts the wrong path, is the taste of the happiness of wealth and gain, auspicious for the rise of prosperity.

1170.

1170.

Saddhādiguṇavodānaṃ, ajjhāsayavikāsanaṃ;

Satācāraparikkhāro, tanucetovibhūsanaṃ.

It is the purification of the qualities beginning with faith, the development of one's inclinations, the equipment for the conduct of the good, an adornment for the subtle mind.

1171.

1171.

Appamaññāpadaṭṭhānaṃ, appameyyena vaṇṇitaṃ;

Mahāpurisacārittaṃ, sapadānaṃ mahesinā.

The foundation of the immeasurables, praised by the Immeasurable One; the conduct of the Great Man, praised with its accounts by the Great Seer.

1172.

1172.

Dhammādhigatabhogānaṃ[M 0.0100], sārādānamanuttaraṃ;

Mahattādhigamūpāyaṃ, lokasantatikāraṇaṃ.

For those who have gained wealth through the Dhamma, it is the unsurpassed taking of the essence, a means for attaining greatness, a cause of the world's continuity.

1173.

1173.

Atthakārī ca sammāhaṃ, pariccāgasamāyuto;

Attano ca paresañca, hitāya paṭipannakā.

Rightly, I am one who acts for welfare, endowed with generosity, one who has undertaken the practice for the benefit of myself and others.

1174.

1174.

Ujumaddavacittosmi, kālussiyavinissaṭo;

Pāpasaṃklesavimukho, pāṇabhūtānukampako.

I have an upright and gentle mind; I am freed from impurity, averse to evil defilements, and compassionate toward living beings.

1175.

1175.

Sīlavantapatiṭṭhosmi[V 0.0107], kapaṇānaṃ parāyaṇo;

Buddhasāsanupaṭṭhāko, ñātimittopajīviko.

I am established in virtue, a refuge for the wretched; a supporter of the Buddha's Dispensation, one who supports relatives and friends.

1176.

1176.

Dānavossaggasammukho,

Saṃvibhāgarato sukhī;

Kapparukkhova phalito,

Jāto lokābhivaḍḍhiyā.

Devoted to giving and relinquishment, delighting in sharing, joyful; like a wish-fulfilling tree laden with fruit, born for the world's increase.

1177.

1177.

Pihitāpāyamaggosmi, maggadvāramapārutaṃ;

Sampattā sabbasampatti, daliddassa manāpikaṃ.

The path to states of woe is closed to me, the door to the noble path is open; all attainments are reached, and I am pleasing to the destitute.

1178.

1178.

“Saṃsāraddhānapātheyyaṃ, sabbadukkhavinodanaṃ;

Subandhaṃ mama sabbattha, gahito ca kaṭaggaho”.

“Provision for the journey of saṃsāra, eliminating all suffering; my good bond is secured everywhere, and a firm grasp has been taken.”

1179.

1179.

Evaṃ dānaguṇaṃ nānappakārena vicintayaṃ;

Bhāveti dāyakoyogī, cāgānussatibhāvanaṃ.

Thus, reflecting in various ways on the qualities of giving, the giving yogi cultivates the development of the recollection of generosity.

1180.

1180.

Saddhaṃ sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgaṃ, paññaṃ paṇḍitajātiko;

Sampādayitvā saddhamme, devatāyo anussare.

Faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom—the wise one, having perfected these qualities in the True Dhamma, recollects the deities.

1181.

1181.

Cātumahārājikā ca, tāvatiṃsā ca yāmakā;

Tusitā ceva nimmānaratino vasavattino.

The Four Great Kings, the Thirty-three, the Yama deities, the Tusita deities, the Nimmānarati deities, and the Vasavatti deities.

1182.

1182.

Taduttariñca ye devā, dibbakāyamadhiṭṭhitā;

Tepi saddhādidhammesu, cirakālaṃ patiṭṭhitā.

And those deities beyond, abiding in divine bodies, they too are long established in faith and other qualities.

1183.

1183.

Susamāhitasaṅkappā, dānasīladhurandharā;

Dhammamaggamadhiṭṭhāya, hirottappapurakkhatā.

With well-composed intentions, foremost in giving and morality, established on the path of Dhamma, preceded by conscience and fear of wrongdoing.

1184.

1184.

Taṃ [M 0.0101] lokamupapannāse, sassirīkaṃ parāyaṇaṃ;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino.

Reborn in that world, glorious and supreme, endowed with psychic powers, radiant, handsome, and renowned.

1185.

1185.

Dibbasampattisampattā, nānābhogasamappitā;

Pālento dīghamaddhānaṃ, anubhonti mahāsukhaṃ.

Possessed of divine prosperity, furnished with various enjoyments, ruling for a long time, they experience great happiness.

1186.

1186.

Te [V 0.0108] sabbepi ca mayhampi, vijjanti anupāyino;

Saddhādikusalā dhammā, devadhammāti vissutā.

And all those skillful qualities of faith and the like, renowned as divine qualities, are also found in me, unfailingly.

1187.

1187.

Saddhammaguṇasampatti-dātā maṅgalanāyikā;

Dullabhāpi ca me laddhā, saddhā sugatasāsane.

The giver of the wealth of the True Dhamma’s virtues, the leader to auspiciousness; even though rare, she has been attained by me—faith in the Sugata's Dispensation.

1188.

1188.

Vajjopavādarahito, pāpakammaparammukho;

Parisuddhasamācāro, pasannāmalacetano.

Free from reproach, turning away from evil deeds; pure in conduct, with a serene and stainless mind.

1189.

1189.

Niccamohitasotosmi,

Tathāgatasubhāsite;

Sutabhājanabhūto ca,

Satimā susamāhito.

Ever immersed in the stream of the Tathāgata's well-spoken words, a vessel of learning, mindful and well-composed.

1190.

1190.

Maccheramalanittiṇṇo, lobhakkhandhavimuccito;

Opānabhūto lokasmiṃ, vissaṭṭhasukhayācano.

Crossed over the stain of stinginess, freed from the mass of greed; having become a wellspring in the world, one who is generous and easily entreated.

1191.

1191.

Vatthuttayamahatte ca, hitāhitavinicchaye;

Paññā vatthusabhāve ca, tikhiṇā mama vattati.

My wisdom is sharp concerning the greatness of the Triple Gem, in discerning benefit and harm, and regarding the true nature of things.

1192.

1192.

Samārādhitasaddhammo, katapuññamahussavo;

Devadhammasamiddhosmi, kalyāṇacaritākaro.

Having perfectly fulfilled the True Dhamma, having made a great festival of merit, I am enriched with divine qualities, a mine of virtuous conduct.

1193.

1193.

Devatāhi samānohaṃ, guṇālaṅkārabhūsito;

Hatthapattā ca deviddhi, nipphannā dibbasampadā.

I am equal to the deities, adorned with the ornament of virtues; divine power has come to hand, divine accomplishment is achieved.

1194.

1194.

Devasāmaññamiccevaṃ, cintento guṇamattano;

Bhāveti guṇasampanno, devatānussatiṃ paraṃ.

Thus reflecting on his own qualities and his commonality with the deities, the virtuous one cultivates the supreme recollection of deities.

1195.

1195.

Jātidhammā jarābyādhisokopāyāsabhañjite;

Anicce dukkhenatte ca, nibbinnopadhisambhave.

Subject to birth, broken by old age, disease, sorrow, and despair; seeing impermanence, suffering, and non-self, one is disenchanted with the arising of the substrates.

1196.

1196.

Virāgo [M 0.0102] ca nirodho ca, cāgo mutti anālayo;

Yoyamādānanissaggo, nibbānamiti vuccati.

Dispassion, cessation, relinquishment, release, and non-attachment—this abandoning of grasping is called Nibbāna.

1197.

1197.

Upasantamidaṃ [V 0.0109] ṭhānamiti cinteti paṇḍito;

Anupādānasaṃkliṭṭhamasaṅkhāramanāsavaṃ.

The wise reflect: 'This state is peaceful—unstained by clinging, unconditioned, and without taints.'

1198.

1198.

Appamāṇaṃ paṇītañca, sivaṃ paramamaccutaṃ;

Anantaguṇamaccanta-mavikāramanāmayaṃ.

Boundless, sublime, auspicious, supreme, deathless—infinite in virtue, utterly unchangeable, free from affliction.

1199.

1199.

Khemaṃ taṃ pārimatīra-mahāyanakaraṃ paraṃ;

Tāṇaṃ leṇañca dīpañca, patiṭṭhānaṃ parāyaṇaṃ.

That is the safe, further shore, the maker of the great vehicle, the supreme; it is protection, shelter, an island, a support, and the final resort.

1200.

1200.

Vaṭṭānubandhavicchedo, bhavataṇhāvisosanaṃ;

Sabbūpadhisamugghāto, dukkhanibbāpanaṃ sukhaṃ.

The severing of the cycle's continuity, the drying up of craving for existence, the uprooting of all substrates, the extinguishing of suffering, which is bliss.

1201.

1201.

Sabbapāpavināsoyaṃ, sabbaklesavisodhanaṃ;

Sokopāyāsasantāpabhayabheravamocanaṃ.

The destruction of all evil, the purification of all defilements, the release from sorrow, despair, anguish, fear, and dread.

1202.

1202.

Palibodhasamucchedo, papañcaviniveṭhanaṃ;

Sabbasaṅkhārasamatho, sabbalokavinissaṭo.

Cutting off all encumbrances, unraveling proliferation, stilling all formations, escaping from all the world.

1203.

1203.

Pārisuddhikarā dhātu, bhavanissaraṇaṃ padaṃ;

Uttamāriyasampatti, anomamamataṃ padaṃ.

The element that makes for perfect purity, the state of escape from becoming; the supreme Noble attainment, the incomparable deathless state.

1204.

1204.

Sabbathā bhaddamatulaṃ, nibbānamiti passato;

Upasamānussatīti, bhāvanāyaṃ pavuccati.

For one who sees Nibbāna as in every way auspicious and incomparable, this development is called the recollection of peace.

1205.

1205.

Sattānussatimiccevaṃ, bhāvento pana paṇḍito;

Pāmojjabahulo hoti, pasanno buddhasāsane.

Thus, the wise one, by developing this recollection of beings, becomes filled with joy, confident in the Buddha's Dispensation.

1206.

1206.

Paṭipassaddhadaratha-mupacārasamādhinā;

Samādhiyati cittañca, parisuddhamanāmayaṃ.

With distress allayed by access concentration, the mind becomes concentrated, purified, and free from affliction.

1207.

1207.

Bhāvanāmayametañca, katvā puññamanappakaṃ;

Vāsanāgatisampatti-bhogabhāgīti vuccati.

Having made this abundant merit consisting of mental development, one is said to be a partaker of good habit-energies, a good destination, attainment, and wealth.

1208.

1208.

Upanissayasampanno, patvā nibbedhamuttamaṃ;

Diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaggiṃ, nibbāpeti anāsavo.

Endowed with supporting conditions, having attained the supreme revulsion, the taintless one extinguishes the fire of suffering in this very life.

1209.

1209.

Lokappavatti [M 0.0103][V 0.0110] cintetvā, maraṇānussatiṃ pana;

Bhāveyya sakamaccantaṃ, cintento maraṇaṃ kathaṃ.

Having reflected on the process of the world, one should then develop the recollection of death, contemplating one's own end and how death comes.

1210.

1210.

Animittamanaññātaṃ, maccānamidha jīvitaṃ;

Kasirañca parittañca, tañca dukkhena saṃyutaṃ.

Unindicated and unknown is the life of mortals here; difficult and brief, it is also conjoined with suffering.

1211.

1211.

Appodakamhi maccheva, bandhamāne rudammukhe;

Maccu gacchati ādāya, pekkhamāne mahājane.

Like a fish in little water, floundering with a weeping face, death comes and takes one away while the great crowd looks on.

1212.

1212.

Purakkhatvāva maraṇaṃ, jāyanti paṭisandhiyaṃ;

Jātā puna marissanti, evaṃdhammā hi pāṇino.

Having placed death right before them, they take rebirth. Having been born, they will die again; for such is the nature of living beings.

1213.

1213.

Yamekarattiṃ paṭhamaṃ, gabbhe vasati mānavo;

Abbhuṭṭhitova so yāti, sa gacchaṃ na nivattati.

From the very first night that a person dwells in the womb, he has set out and is on his way; he goes on without turning back.

1214.

1214.

Sattā maranti gabbhepi, jāyamānā ca dārakā;

Kumārā yobbanappattā, balappattā mahattarā.

Beings die even in the womb, and infants at birth; also youths, those who have reached adolescence, adults in their prime, and the very old.

1215.

1215.

Athāvassaṃ maranteva, jiṇṇā daṇḍaparāyaṇā;

Sūrā puññabalatthāmā, nānābyādhinipīḷitā.

Then, inevitably, they die: the aged who rely on a staff; heroes; those with the strength and power of merit; and those afflicted by various diseases.

1216.

1216.

Ajja suveti maraṇaṃ, pariyesati pāṇino;

Senā yuddhapayātāva, sabbe maccubhayākulā.

Death seeks out living beings, whether today or tomorrow. Like an army that has gone forth to battle, all are agitated by the fear of death.

1217.

1217.

Sattāratanalaṅkārā, caturiddhisamuggatā;

Cakkavattī mahātejā, rājamaṇḍalasobhino.

The mighty wheel-turning monarch of great majesty, beautifying the royal realm, adorned with the seven treasures and endowed with the four psychic powers—

1218.

1218.

Kappuṭṭhānamahāvātā, pātitāva mahāsilā;

Patanti maccuvikkhittā, paro cetāna mānavā.

like great rocks hurled down by the great winds at the end of the aeon, they fall, scattered by death—and other people as well.

1219.

1219.

Yepi dīghāyukā devā, vaṇṇavantā mahiddhikā;

Ānubhāvabalappattā, mahābhogasukhedhino.

Even those devas who are long-lived, beautiful, and of great psychic power, who have attained great might and strength, and who thrive in great wealth and happiness—

1220.

1220.

Tepi maccusamuddhattā, bhavanti bhayasaṃkulā;

Verambhakkhittapakkhīva, mādisesu kathāva kā.

—they too are swept away by death and become filled with fear, like birds tossed about by a Verambha wind. What, then, can be said of those like me?

1221.

1221.

Accantarāyabahulo[V 0.0111], maraṇāhitasambhavo;

Niccaṃ cakkasamāruḷho, lokoyaṃ parivattati.

This world, full of extreme dangers, where birth is linked to death, constantly revolves as if mounted on a wheel.

1222.

1222.

Etthantare [M 0.0104] maraṇassa, vemajjhe mama vattato;

Assāsepi avissaṭṭhe, jīvikā ce kathāva kā.

In this interval before death, while I am in this middle state, when there is no certainty even about a single breath, what can be said of life?

1223.

1223.

Accheraṃ vata lokasmiṃ, khaṇamattampi jīvitaṃ;

Nissitopaddavaṭṭhāne, mahābyasanapīḷite.

How astonishing it is in this world! Life lasts for only a moment, based in a place of calamity, afflicted by great disaster.

1224.

1224.

Addhuvaṃ jīvitaṃ nicca-maccantaṃ maraṇaṃ mama;

Sabhāvo maraṇanteva, viseso pana jīvitaṃ.

My life is uncertain, but my death is certain. Death is indeed my nature; life is but a special interval.

1225.

1225.

Atthamārabbha gacchanto, ādiccova nabhantare;

Maraṇāyābhidhāvanto, vihāyāmi suve suve.

Like the sun moving across the sky towards its setting, I go on, rushing towards death, leaving each day behind me.

1226.

1226.

Vajjhappatto mahācoro,

Niyyātāghātanaṃ yathā;

Maraṇāya payātohaṃ,

Tathevamanivattiyo.

Just as a great robber condemned to death is led to the place of execution, so I go forth towards death, just so, irreversibly.

1227.

1227.

Ambujova vaṅkaghasto, tāṇaleṇavivajjito;

Niccaṃ maccuvasaṃ yanto, vissaṭṭho kimahaṃ care.

Like a lotus swept away by the current, devoid of shelter and refuge, always going under the sway of death—why should I live heedlessly?

1228.

1228.

Ko me hāso kimānando,

Kimahaṃ mohapāruto;

Madappamādavikkhitto,

Vicarāmi niraṅkuso?

What laughter is there for me, what joy? Why, wrapped in delusion, distracted by intoxication and negligence, do I wander about without restraint?

1229.

1229.

Handāhamārabhissāmi, sammāsambuddhasāsane;

Ātāpī pahitatto ca, hirottappasamāhito.

Well now, I will exert myself in the Dispensation of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, ardent and resolute, endowed with shame and fear of wrongdoing.

1230.

1230.

Paṭipattiparo hutvā, pāpadhammaniraṅkato;

Nibbāpayāmi accantaṃ, sabbadukkhahutāvahaṃ.

Having become devoted to the practice, freed from evil states, I will utterly extinguish the fire of all suffering.

1231.

1231.

Itthaṃ [V 0.0112] panattano yogī, maraṇaṃ paṭicintayaṃ;

Maraṇānussatiṃ nāma, bhāvetīti pavuccati.

Thus, a yogi who reflects in this way on his own death is said to be developing the recollection of death.

1232.

1232.

Tadetaṃ [M 0.0105] pana bhāvetvā, upacārasamāhito;

Nibbedabahulo hoti, appamādadhurandharo.

Having developed this and become composed in access concentration, one becomes filled with revulsion and takes up the yoke of diligence.

1233.

1233.

Micchādhammaṃ virājetvā, nandirāganirālayo;

Sabbāsavaparikkhīṇo, pappoti amataṃ padaṃ.

Having become dispassionate towards wrong states, free from attachment to delight and lust, with all taints completely destroyed, one attains the deathless state.

1234.

1234.

Gahetvā pana medhāvī, dvattiṃsākārabhāvanaṃ;

Kareyya tāva pacchā ve, anupubbamabhiṇhaso.

Now, a wise person, having taken up the development of the thirty-two aspects, should practice it forwards and backwards, repeatedly and in due order.

1235.

1235.

Kesā lomā nakhā dantā, taco maṃsaṃ nahāru ca;

Aṭṭhi ca miñja vakkaṃ ca, hadayaṃ yakanaṃ tathā.

Head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin; and flesh and sinews; and bones, bone-marrow, and kidneys; heart, liver, likewise.

1236.

1236.

Kilomaṃ pihaka papphāsaṃ, antaṃ guṇamudariyaṃ;

Matthaluṅgaṃ karīsañca, pittaṃ semhamathāparaṃ.

Pleura, spleen, lungs; intestines, mesentery, gorge; and brain and feces; bile, phlegm, and then the next.

1237.

1237.

Pubbo ca lohitaṃ sedo,

Medo assu vasātha vā;

Kheḷo siṅghāṇikā ceva,

Lasikā muttamiccapi.

And pus, blood, sweat; fat, tears, and skin-grease; saliva and snot; synovial fluid and also urine.

1238.

1238.

Ghanabandhasubhākāra-vipallāsānusārinaṃ;

Yathābhūtāvabodhāya, vibhattāva mahesinā.

For the sake of a true understanding by those who follow the perversion of seeing the body as a solid mass and a beautiful form, these parts have been analyzed by the Great Sage.

1239.

1239.

Kāye bāttiṃsa koṭṭhāsā,

Kuṇapāva samussitā;

Sāragayhūpagāpetā,

Dhikkatā dhīrahīḷitā.

In the body are thirty-two parts, piled up like a corpse, filled with what is foul, despised and scorned by the wise.

1240.

1240.

Asubhāva paṭikkūlā, jegucchā sucivajjitā;

Ninditā cakkhumantehi, andhabālopalāḷitā.

Foul, repulsive, and disgusting, they are devoid of purity. Censured by the clear-eyed, they are cherished only by blind fools.

1241.

1241.

Vicittachavisañchannā[V 0.0113], tacabhattasamohitā;

Parissavaparikliṭṭhā, kuthitā pūtigandhitā.

Covered with variegated skin, a deluding bag of hide, defiled by its own oozing, it is putrid and foul-smelling.

1242.

1242.

Dhoviyantāpi [M 0.0106] satataṃ, ajahantā malassavaṃ;

Sugandhānuvilittāpi, duggandhapariṇāmino.

Though constantly washed, it does not give up its outflow of filth. Though anointed with perfumes, it ends up with a foul smell.

1243.

1243.

Ahaṃkāramamattena, vissaṭṭhasukhasaṅgahā;

Saṅghāṭaghanasambaddhā, sammohenti mahājanaṃ.

Bound together as a solid composite, these parts delude the great mass of people, who, through their I-making and my-making, have forsaken the acquisition of true happiness.

1244.

1244.

Chandarāgasamūpetā, yattha muḷhā puthujjanā;

Sevanti visamaṃ ghoraṃ, caturāpāyabhāgino.

Endowed with desire and lust, ordinary people are deluded by this. They resort to what is crooked and terrible, thus becoming destined for the four planes of misery.

1245.

1245.

Tattha cittaṃ virājetuṃ, paṭipanno yathākkamaṃ;

Cetovibhāvanatthāya, koṭṭhāsesu vicakkhaṇo.

To make the mind dispassionate towards that, one should practice in due order; for the development of the mind, one should be skilled in the parts.

1246.

1246.

Vacasā manasā ceva, yathāvuttānusārato;

Anulomapaṭilomaṃ, sajjhāyitvā tato paraṃ.

With speech and mind, according to what has been said, having recited in forward and reverse order, one then proceeds.

1247.

1247.

Vaṇṇasaṇṭhānadisato, vavatthapeyya paṇḍito;

Tatokāsaparicchedā, paccekaṃ tu yathākkamaṃ.

A wise one should define by color, shape, and direction; then, by delimiting the space, each part in due order.

1248.

1248.

Vaṇṇasaṇṭhānagandhā ca,

Āsayokāsato tato;

Vibhāveyyāsubhākāra-

Mekekasmiṃ tu pañcadhā.

Color, shape, and smell, and also location and spatial orientation: one should discriminate the unattractive aspects in each individually, in five ways.

1249.

1249.

Dasadhābhogamiccevaṃ, katvā bhāvayato pana;

Santibhūtā pakāsenti, rathacakkārasādisā.

Having thus made the tenfold application, for one who develops, they reveal themselves as peaceful, like the spokes of a wheel.

1250.

1250.

Hitvā appaguṇe tattha, gaṇhaṃ suppaguṇaṃ budho;

Appanaṃ paṭibhāgañca, pappotekekavatthusu.

Having abandoned the inferior qualities there, the wise one grasps the superior qualities and attains absorption and the counterpart sign in each object.

1251.

1251.

Asubhākāramārabbha, bhāvanā ce pavattati;

Kammaṭṭhānaṃ paṭikkūlaṃ, paṭhamajjhānikaṃ siyā.

If meditation proceeds, having begun with the aspect of unattractiveness, then the repulsive meditation subject would be suitable for the first jhāna.

1252.

1252.

Nīlādivaṇṇamārabbha, paṭibhāgo yadā tadā;

Nīlādikasiṇaṃ hutvā, pañcakajjhānikaṃ bhave.

When the counterpart sign arises, having begun with colors like blue, it becomes a kasiṇa of blue and so forth, leading to the five jhānas.

1253.

1253.

Lakkhaṇākāramārabbha[V 0.0114], cintanā ce pavattati;

Vipassanākammaṭṭhāna-miti bhāsanti paṇḍitā.

If contemplation proceeds, having begun with the aspect of characteristics, the wise speak of it as insight meditation.

1254.

1254.

Tidhā [M 0.0107] pabhedamiccevaṃ, bhāvento puna buddhimā;

Kāyagatāsatiṃ nāma, bhāvetīti pavuccati.

Thus, the intelligent one, developing it in these three ways, is said to develop mindfulness of the body.

1255.

1255.

Soyamajjhattaṃ nibbinno, bahiddhā ca nirālayo;

Ubbegabahulo yogī, pamādamativattati.

He, disenchanted within and detached from what is outside, the yogi, abounding in spiritual urgency, overcomes negligence.

1256.

1256.

Kāmabandhavinimutto, pāpā medhāvi nissaṭo;

Sacchikatvāna sāmaññaṃ, amataṃ paribhuñjati.

Freed from the bonds of sensuality, the wise one released from evil, having realized recluseship, partakes of the Deathless.

1257.

1257.

Ānāpānassatiṃ nāma, sammāsambuddhavaṇṇitaṃ;

Kammaṭṭhānādhirājānaṃ, bhāvento pana paṇḍito.

The wise one cultivates mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, praised by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the sovereign of meditation subjects.

1258.

1258.

Appanañcopacārañca, samathañca vipassanaṃ;

Lokuttaraṃ lokiyañca, sukhenevādhigacchati.

Absorption and access, serenity and insight, the supramundane and the mundane—one attains them with ease.

1259.

1259.

Sukhumā nipuṇā tikkhā, paripakkā bale ṭhitā;

Bodhipakkhiyadhammā ca, vodāyanti visesato.

Subtle, refined, sharp, fully ripened, and established in strength, the factors of enlightenment become especially purified.

1260.

1260.

Kammaṭṭhāne tathā hettha, gaṇanā anubandhanā;

Phusanā ṭhapanā ceva, sallakkhaṇavivaṭṭanā.

Herein, likewise, in this meditation subject, there are counting, following, touching, establishing, discerning, and turning away.

1261.

1261.

Pārisuddhi tato pacchā, tesañca paṭipassanā;

Iccevamaṭṭhadhā bhedā, mātikāyaṃ pakāsitā.

After that, purification, and their retrospection; thus, the eightfold division is revealed in the matrix.

1262.

1262.

Vibhattā satipaṭṭhāna-vasā soḷasadhā tato;

Ānāpānappabhedena, bhinnā dvattiṃsadhā puna.

Thereafter, it is divided sixteenfold according to the foundations of mindfulness; then, by the divisions of in-and-out breathing, it is again divided thirty-twofold.

1263.

1263.

Tameva pariyādāya, samathañca vipassanaṃ;

Mahattavepullagataṃ, bhāveyya satimā kathaṃ.

Having fully mastered that, how should a mindful one develop serenity and insight to greatness and abundance?

1264.

1264.

Ānāpānaṃ pariggayha, pavivitto rahogato;

Gaṇeyya paṭhamaṃ tāva, nisinno sukhamāsane.

Having taken up in-and-out breathing, secluded and gone to a solitary place, one should first count, seated on a comfortable seat.

1265.

1265.

Pañcannaṃ [V 0.0115] na ṭhapetabbaṃ, heṭṭhā na dasatopari;

Netabbamanupubbena, gaṇetabbamakhaṇḍitaṃ.

One should not set the count below five, nor above ten; it should be conducted progressively and counted uninterruptedly.

1266.

1266.

Anto [M 0.0108] bahi ca vikkhepa-makatvāna punappunaṃ;

Phuṭṭhaṭṭhānamhi satimā, anubandheyya mānasaṃ.

Without creating distraction inside or outside, again and again, the mindful one should keep the mind closely following the point of contact.

1267.

1267.

Nāsikaggottaroṭṭhe ca, katvābhogaṃ tatoparaṃ;

Satatassāsasamphassaṃ, āvajjantassa yogino.

Having applied attention to the tip of the nose or the upper lip, thereafter, the yogi, by adverting, attends to the constant touch of the breath.

1268.

1268.

Puthulaṃ vātha dīghaṃ vā, maṇḍalaṃ vātha vitthataṃ;

Tārakādisamākāraṃ, nimittaṃ tattha jāyati.

Whether broad or long, round or extended, a sign arises there resembling a star or other forms.

1269.

1269.

Cittaṃ samāhitaṃ hoti, upacārasamādhinā;

Upaklesā pahiyyanti, paṭibhāge samuṭṭhite.

The mind becomes concentrated with access concentration; defilements are abandoned when the counterpart sign arises.

1270.

1270.

Nimitte ṭhapayaṃ cittaṃ, tato pāpeti appanaṃ;

Pañcajjhānavasenāyaṃ, samathe bhāvanānayo.

Fixing the mind on the sign, one then attains absorption. This is the method of development in serenity by way of the five jhānas.

1271.

1271.

Ārabhitvābhinivesa-mānāpāne punāparo;

Ajjhattañca bahiddhā ca, tato tadanusārato.

Having initiated application to in-and-out breathing, and then another, both internally and externally, and thereafter in accordance with that.

1272.

1272.

Bhūmidhamme yathābhūtaṃ, vipassitvā visārado;

Appetānuttarajjhāna-mayaṃ suddhivipassanā.

Having seen with insight the phenomena of the planes as they actually are, the expert attains the purity of insight consisting of unsurpassed jhāna.

1273.

1273.

Ānāpānasamāpattiṃ, katvā pādakamuttaraṃ;

Bhāventassa vasenāhu, nayaṃ soḷasadhā kathaṃ.

Having made the attainment of in-and-out breathing the supreme foundation, by way of one who develops it, the sixteenfold method is explained.

1274.

1274.

Dīghamassāsapassāsā, rassaṃ vātha tathā dvayaṃ;

Satimā matisampanno, paṭhamaṃ parigaṇhati.

Long in-breaths and out-breaths, or short ones, or both likewise—the mindful one endowed with wisdom first comprehends them.

1275.

1275.

Ādimajjhāvasānaṃ tu, karonto viditaṃ tathā;

Samāhito sabbakāya-paṭisaṃvedi sikkhati.

Making known the beginning, middle, and end, thus composed, one trains experiencing the entire body.

1276.

1276.

Tato te eva saṅkhāre, passambhentoparūpari;

Vutto passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ sikkhatīti ca.

Then, calming those very formations progressively, it is said: 'One trains, calming the bodily formation.'

1277.

1277.

Ānāpānasaticcevaṃ[V 0.0116], kāyasaṅkhāranissitā;

Kāyānupassanā nāma, catudhāpi ca bhāsitā.

Thus, mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, which is dependent on bodily formations, is called contemplation of the body, and it is also spoken of in four ways.

1278.

1278.

Sampayuttena [M 0.0109] ñāṇena, pītimālambaṇena ca;

Vipassanāya samathe, kubbanto pākaṭaṃ sukhaṃ.

With associated knowledge and with joy as the object, one makes happiness manifest in insight and serenity.

1279.

1279.

Vedanāsaññāsaṅkhāte, cittasaṅkhārake tathā;

Pītādipaṭisaṃvedī, sikkhatīti pavuccati.

One who experiences joy and so on, with regard to what are termed feeling and perception, and likewise mental formations, is said to be 'one who trains'.

1280.

1280.

Thūle te eva saṅkhāre, sametuṃ paribhāvayaṃ;

Vutto “passambhayaṃ cittaṃ, saṅkhāraṃ sikkhatī”ti ca.

Developing to calm those very gross formations, it is said: 'One trains, calming the mental formation.'

1281.

1281.

Tassā taṃtaṃmukhenettha, sampajjanavisesato;

Vedanānupassanāya, catudhā samudīritā.

Here, by means of its various aspects and through special clear comprehension, the contemplation of feeling is taught in four ways.

1282.

1282.

Appento paccavekkhanto, bujjhanto ca pakāsitaṃ;

Karonto mānasaṃ citta-paṭisaṃvedi sikkhati.

Attaining, reviewing, and understanding what is revealed, while directing the mind, one trains experiencing the mind.

1283.

1283.

Tamevābhippamodento, sappītikasamādhinā;

“Abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ, sikkhatī”ti pavuccati.

Delighting in just that with concentration accompanied by joy, one is said to train thus: 'Gladdening the mind.'

1284.

1284.

Appanāyopacārena, tamevātha samādahaṃ;

Yogī “samādahaṃ cittaṃ, sikkhatī”ti pakāsito.

By means of absorption and access, then concentrating just that, the yogi is declared as one who trains thus: 'Concentrating the mind.'

1285.

1285.

Paccanīkehi vikkhambha-samucchedehi mocayaṃ;

Tathā “vimocayaṃ cittaṃ, sikkhatī”tipi bhāsito.

Liberating the mind from opposing forces by suppression and eradication, he is likewise spoken of as one who trains thus: 'Liberating the mind.'

1286.

1286.

Ānāpānaṃ pabhedāya, kammaṭṭhānaṃ yathārahaṃ;

Cittānupassanā nāma, pavattāyaṃ catubbidhā.

For the analysis of in-and-out breathing, the meditation subject is appropriately called 'contemplation of mind'; this proceeds in four ways.

1287.

1287.

Vipassanāyaniccānu-gatattā hi visesato;

Vipassanto aniccānu-passī sikkhati paṇḍito.

Indeed, because insight is especially characterized by the pursuit of impermanence, the wise one trains, seeing with insight and contemplating impermanence.

1288.

1288.

Tato virāgānupassī, nibbinditvā virājayaṃ;

Tathā nirodhānupassī, bhūmidhamme nirodhayaṃ.

Then, contemplating dispassion, having become disenchanted, one causes fading away; likewise, contemplating cessation, one causes the phenomena of the planes to cease.

1289.

1289.

Pakkhandanapariccāgapaṭinissaggato [V 0.0117] pana;

Paṭinissaggānupassī, sikkhatīti pavuccati.

Through leaping forth, abandonment, and relinquishment, one is said to train, contemplating relinquishment.

1290.

1290.

Ānāpānamukheneva[M 0.0110], bhūmidhammavipassanā;

Dhammānupassanā nāma, bhāsitevaṃ catubbidhā.

Insight into the phenomena of the planes by means of in-and-out breathing is indeed called the contemplation of phenomena, thus taught as fourfold.

1291.

1291.

Iti soḷasadhākāraṃ, sikkhattayapatiṭṭhitaṃ;

Catubbidhampi pūreti, satipaṭṭhānabhāvanaṃ.

Thus, the sixteen-aspected development of the fourfold foundations of mindfulness, established in the threefold training, is also fulfilled.

1292.

1292.

Pariggayha satiñceva-mussāhanto vipassanaṃ;

Dvattiṃsākārabhedehi, satokārīti vuccati.

Thus having grasped mindfulness and striving for insight, one is called 'one who acts mindfully' by means of the thirty-two aspects.

1293.

1293.

Itthañca gaṇanādīhi, bhāvetvā samathaṃ tato;

Vipassanādhivacanaṃ, katvā sallakkhaṇaṃ puna.

And thus, having developed serenity by counting and so on, then, having made insight the principal designation, one again discerns the characteristics.

1294.

1294.

Patvā vivaṭṭanāmaggaṃ, pārisuddhiphale ṭhito;

Paccavekkhaṇasaṅkhātaṃ, pappoti satipassanaṃ.

Having reached the path of turning away, standing in the fruit of purity, one attains the mindfulness and insight known as reviewing.

1295.

1295.

Ānāpānasaticcevamasesaṃ paripūritā;

Sākāraṃ sappabhedañca, bhāvitāti pavuccati.

Mindfulness of breathing, thus completely fulfilled with its aspects and distinctions, is said to be developed.

1296.

1296.

Ānāpānasamādhimetamatulaṃ buddhāpadānuttamaṃ,

Pāpaklesarajoharaṃ sukhamukhaṃ dukkhagginibbāpanaṃ;

Bhāvetvā satisampajaññavipulā vikkhepaviddhaṃsakā,

Pappontuttaramuttamāmatapadaṃ bodhittayabyāpakaṃ.

Having cultivated this immeasurable concentration of mindfulness of breathing—the unsurpassed achievement of the Buddhas, which removes the dust of evil defilements, is the door to happiness, and extinguishes the fire of suffering—they who are abundant in mindfulness and clear comprehension, destroyers of distraction, attain the ultimate, supreme, deathless state that pervades the triple enlightenment.

1297.

1297.

Buddhaṃ dhammañca saṅghaṃ puthunanamahitaṃ suddhasīlaṃ sudānaṃ,

Dhammaṭṭhā devatāyopasamatha maraṇaṃ kāyamānañcapānaṃ;

Paññattārabbhayāyaṃ satisamavahitā bodhimaggodayāya,

Sāyaṃ saddhammanettī sahitasivaguṇā sevitabbādarena.

The Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, revered by many people; pure virtue and generous giving; deities established in the Dhamma; the pacification of death, body, conceit, and breath; this is proclaimed for the sake of fearlessness, with mindfulness well-established for the arising of the path to enlightenment—this guide of the true Dhamma, endowed with peaceful qualities, should be followed with reverence.

Iti nāmarūpaparicchede dasānussativibhāgo nāma

Thus ends the section named the Analysis of the Ten Recollections in the Determination of Mind and Matter.

Navamo paricchedo.

The Ninth Chapter.

10. Dasamo paricchedo

10. The Tenth Chapter.

Sesakammaṭṭhānavibhāgo

The Division of the Remaining Meditation Subjects.

1298.

1298.

Byāpādādīnavaṃ [M 0.0111][V 0.0118] disvā, khemabhāvañca khantiyaṃ;

Appamaññā tu bhāvento, vineyya paṭighaṃ kathaṃ.

Having seen the danger in ill will and the state of security in patience, how can one, developing the boundless states, subdue resentment?

1299.

1299.

Cetosantāpano kodho,

Sampasādavikopano;

Virūpabībhacchakaro,

Mukhavaṇṇappadhaṃsano.

Anger inflames the mind, it disturbs serenity, makes one deformed and repulsive, and destroys the facial complexion.

1300.

1300.

Sīlakālussiyuppādo, cittavikkhepasambhavo;

Paññāpajjotaviddhaṃsī, paṭipattivibandhako.

It is the arising of moral impurity, the source of mental distraction, the destroyer of the lamp of wisdom, and the obstructer of the path of practice.

1301.

1301.

Apāyekāyano maggo, pāpakaṇṭakabandhako;

Dhammamaggasamucchedī, maggadvārapidhānako.

It is a path leading only to the lower realms, bound by evil thorns; it destroys the path of Dhamma, blocking the door to the path.

1302.

1302.

Yasovaṇṇavisaṅkhāro, guṇamūlappabhañjako;

Dukkhadhammasamodhāno, byasanopaddavākaro.

It is the destruction of fame and complexion, the shattering of the roots of virtue; a confluence of states of suffering, it causes calamity and misfortune.

1303.

1303.

Dunnimittamidaṃ jātaṃ, sabbasampattidhaṃsanaṃ;

Dhūmaketusamuppādo, sabbalokavināsako.

This is an evil omen born, destructive of all prosperity; it is the arising of a comet, a destroyer of the whole world.

1304.

1304.

Sabbakalyāṇadhammānaṃ, avamaṅgalamuṭṭhitaṃ;

Hitārambhasamugghātī, antarāyasamāgamo.

It is an inauspicious thing arisen for all wholesome qualities; it is the destruction of beneficial undertakings, the coming together of obstacles.

1305.

1305.

Sabbākārapaṭikkūlaṃ, sabbaviddesakāraṇaṃ;

Vipattimukhamuppannaṃ, amittajanapatthitaṃ.

It is repulsive in all aspects, the cause of all enmity; it has arisen as the gateway to ruin, desired by hostile people.

1306.

1306.

Sapattakaraṇaṃ [V 0.0119] ghoraṃ, sabbānatthavidhāyakaṃ;

Bhayamantarato jātaṃ, taṃ jano nāvabujjhati.

It is dreadful, making one a rival, causing all kinds of harm; it is fear born from within, which people do not understand.

1307.

1307.

Khuradhāraṃ lihantāva, gilantāva hutāsanaṃ;

Tittalābuṃva khādantā, gaṇhantādittamāyudhaṃ.

As if licking a razor's edge, as if swallowing fire, as if eating a bitter gourd, as if grasping a burning weapon.

1308.

1308.

Byāpādamattasambhava-mattaghaññāya [M 0.0112] kevalaṃ;

Upalāḷenti dummedhā, ghoramāsīvisaṃ yathā.

Fools cherish that which is born merely of ill will, solely for their own destruction, like a dreadful venomous snake.

1309.

1309.

Dosatejena rukkhova, susirāruḷhapāvako;

Antonudayhamānāpi, vipphandanti vighātino.

Like a tree with fire having entered its hollow, by the heat of hatred, though burning inwardly, the tormentors writhe.

1310.

1310.

Nāvabujjhanti dummedhā, cetosaṅkappavāyunā;

Ukkāmukhāmivāditta-mujjalantā punappunaṃ.

Fools do not understand, blazing up again and again like a burning firebrand, driven by the wind of mental conception.

1311.

1311.

Bhayamaggasamāruḷhā, khemamaggavirodhino;

Byāpannā kibbisākiṇṇā, atthadvayavirodhino.

Having embarked on the path of fear, opposing the path to safety, malicious, filled with wickedness, they obstruct both kinds of benefit.

1312.

1312.

Anāthā sallakāviddhā, visaṭṭā anusocino;

Andhā viya migāraññe, bhamanti hatacakkhukā.

Helpless, pierced by a dart, abandoned, grieving; like blind deer in the forest, they wander, their eyes destroyed.

1313.

1313.

Asaṃvihitakammantā, bālā kodhavasānugā;

Khippaṃ lakkhiṃ pariccattā, yasobhogehi dhaṃsare.

Fools, following anger's sway, whose actions are not well-arranged, having quickly abandoned their fortune, are ruined in fame and possessions.

1314.

1314.

Duppaṭippāditārambhā, kodhasaṅkhobhamohitā;

Dhammāmatarasassādaṃ, na vindanti aviddasu.

The unwise, whose undertakings are hard to accomplish, bewildered by the agitation of anger, do not find the taste of the deathless Dhamma.

1315.

1315.

Bahvādīnavamicceva-manto byādhimivuṭṭhitaṃ;

Jātānalamivucchaṅge, ajjhupekkhanti dujjanā.

The wicked disregard it, though it has many dangers, like a sickness arisen within, like a fire arisen in one's lap.

1316.

1316.

Codayamānā dukkhehi, klesāciṇṇamalīmahā;

Pāpakammehi pūrentā, senti maccupathe ciraṃ.

Being urged on by sufferings, greatly stained by accumulated defilements, filling themselves with evil deeds, they lie long on the path of death.

1317.

1317.

Tamevaṃ paṭisaṅkhāya, paṭighaṃ pana yoniso;

Vāḷamigaṃva dhāvantaṃ, āvisantaṃva rakkhasaṃ.

Therefore, having reflected thus, one should wisely abandon resentment, which is like a running wild beast or an entering demon.

1318.

1318.

Pāvakaṃva [V 0.0120] paribyuḷhaṃ, bhāyamānassa yogino;

Sotthibhāvāya khemanta-mupaññattaṃ mahesinā.

For the fearful yogi, for the sake of well-being, the great seer taught the path to safety, which is like a fire brought under control.

1319.

1319.

Mātā kalyāṇadhammānaṃ, khamā nāma mahiddhikā;

Samappavatti sattesu, sabbasampattisādhikā.

Forbearance, the mother of wholesome qualities, is of great power; acting impartially towards beings, she is the accomplisher of all success.

1320.

1320.

Kodhānalajalāseko[M 0.0113],

Sokopāyāsanāsanaṃ;

Āghātasallaniddhārī,

Upanāhavimocanaṃ.

It is the sprinkling of water on the fire of anger, the destruction of sorrow and distress, the extractor of the dart of hate, and the release from resentment.

1321.

1321.

Vaṇṇakittisamuṭṭhānaṃ, guṇamūlābhisevanaṃ;

Apārutamukhaṃveta-matthadvayasamiddhiyā.

It is the arising of beauty and fame, the cultivation of the roots of virtue; this is an open door for the accomplishment of both aims.

1322.

1322.

Vighātapariyādāna-māsavānamasesato;

Paṭipassambhanaṃ ceto-pītikaraṇacandanaṃ.

The complete exhaustion of vexation and the taints, without remainder; it is a tranquilizer, the sandalwood that gladdens the heart.

1323.

1323.

Sabbadukkhasamugghāti, sukhupaṭṭhānamuttamaṃ;

Byasanodayavicchedo, bhayabheravaniggamo.

The uprooting of all suffering, the supreme establishment of happiness; the cutting off of the arising of misfortune, the departure from fear and terror.

1324.

1324.

Cetopasādasandhāno, pāsādikaphalāvaho;

Pavaro bodhisambhāro, narānaranisevito.

It is the establishment of mental clarity, bringing about pleasing results; the excellent requisite for enlightenment, frequented by humans and non-humans.

1325.

1325.

Pāpakantāranitthāro, caturāpāyarodhako;

Dvārāvāpuraṇañcetaṃ, devalokūpapattiyā.

It is the crossing over the wilderness of evil, the obstruction to the four woeful states; and this is the opening of the door to rebirth in the celestial world.

1326.

1326.

Paññāsīlasamādhānaṃ, paṭipattivisodhano;

Piyaṅkaro sommabhāvo, dullabho bahupatthito.

The foundation of wisdom and virtue, the purifier of practice; an endearing and gentle nature, difficult to obtain, much desired.

1327.

1327.

Klesasaṅkhobhavikkhepa-vipphandapaṭibandhanaṃ;

Titikkhāguṇamakkhāta-mārakkhavidhimattano.

The prevention of agitation, distraction, and wavering born of defilements; the quality of patience is declared to be one's own method of protection.
