With a desirable object, wholesome results arise in every way; with an undesirable object, unwholesome results arise—this rule is declared.

99.

99.

Tatthāpi atiiṭṭhamhi, tadārammaṇatīraṇaṃ;

Somanassayutaṃ iṭṭhamajjhattamhi upekkhitaṃ.

Therein, with a highly desirable object, registration and investigating are accompanied by joy; with a neutrally desirable object, they are accompanied by equanimity.

100.

100.

Gocaretiparittamhi[V 0.0011], atiappāyuke pana;

Bhavaṅgameva calati, moghavāroti so kato.

When the object is very slight, or when its duration is very short, the life-continuum merely vibrates; this is called a vain occurrence.

101.

101.

Voṭṭhabbanaṃ parittamhi, dvattikkhattuṃ pavattati;

Tato bhavaṅgapātova, sopi moghoti vuccati.

When the object is limited, determining proceeds two or three times, then there is a lapse into the life-continuum—that too is called vain.

102.

102.

Javanañca mahantamhi, javitvāna tato paraṃ;

Na sambhoti tadālambaṃ, sopi moghoti vuccati.

And when the object is great, after impulsion has occurred, registration does not arise thereafter—that too is called vain.

103.

103.

Gocaretimahantamhi, atidīghāyuke pana;

Sambhoti ca tadālambaṃ, sampuṇṇoti pavuccati.

When the object is very great, and when its duration is very long, registration arises; this is called a complete process.

104.

104.

Gocaretimahantamhi, tadārammaṇasambhavo;

Pañcadvāre manodvāre, vibhūte pana gocare.

The arising of registration occurs when the object is very great in the five-door process, and when the object is distinct in the mind-door process.

105.

105.

Kāmāvacarasattānaṃ[M 0.0010], kāmāvacaragocare;

Parittajavanesveva, tadārammaṇamuddise.

For beings of the sensual sphere, with a sensual-sphere object, one should designate registration only in the case of sense-sphere impulsions.

106.

106.

Nātitikkhe nātisīghe, nātitejussade jave;

Samamandappavattamhi, tadārammaṇamicchitaṃ.

Not too sharp, not too swift, not with excessive intensity of impulsion; when it proceeds evenly and gently, registration is to be expected.

107.

107.

Sukhopetaṃ tadālambaṃ, upekkhākriyato paraṃ;

Na hotupekkhāsahitaṃ, sukhitakriyato tathā.

Registration accompanied by joy does not arise after functional consciousness accompanied by equanimity; likewise, that accompanied by equanimity does not arise after functional consciousness accompanied by joy.

108.

108.

Na hoti domanassamhā, somanassikamānasaṃ;

Tadārammaṇamaññañca, bhavaṅgaṃ cuti vā tathā.

Consciousness accompanied by joy does not arise from displeasure; nor, likewise, do registration, the life-continuum, or the death-consciousness.

109.

109.

Rajjanādivasenettha, javanākusalaṃ bhave;

Kusalaṃ pana sambhoti, saddhāpaññādisambhave.

Here, unwholesome impulsion arises by way of attachment and so on; but wholesome impulsion arises from the presence of faith, wisdom, and so on.

110.

110.

Tadeva vītarāgānaṃ, kriyā nāma pavuccati;

Avipākatamāpannaṃ, vaṭṭamūlaparikkhayā.

For those free from passion, that same [wholesome consciousness] is called 'functional,' having become non-resultant through the exhaustion of the root of the cycle of existence.

111.

111.

Appanājavanaṃ sesaṃ, mahaggatamanuttaraṃ;

Chabbīsati yathāyogaṃ, appanāvīthiyaṃ bhave.

The remaining impulsion is absorption, sublime and supramundane. Twenty-six types, as is appropriate, may occur in an absorption process.

112.

112.

Parikammaṃ [V 0.0012] karontassa, kasiṇādikagocare;

Susamāhitacittassa, upacārasamādhinā.

For one who performs preliminary work on objects such as a kasiṇa, with a well-concentrated mind, through access concentration,

113.

113.

Parikammopacārānulomagotrabhuto paraṃ;

Pañcamaṃ vā catutthaṃ vā, javanaṃ hoti appanā.

After preliminary work, access, conformity, and change-of-lineage, the fifth or the fourth impulsion becomes absorption.

114.

114.

Puthujjanāna sekkhānaṃ, kāmapuññatihetuto;

Tihetukāmakriyato, vītarāgānamappanā.

For ordinary people and trainees, absorption arises from three-rooted wholesome consciousness of the sense-sphere; for those free from passion, from three-rooted functional consciousness of the sense-sphere.

115.

115.

Tatrāpi sukhitajavaṃ, sukhitadvayato paraṃ;

Upekkhitamhā sambhoti, upekkhekaggatāyutaṃ.

Therein, impulsion accompanied by joy arises after the two accompanied by joy; from that which is accompanied by equanimity arises impulsion conjoined with equanimity and one-pointedness.

116.

116.

Pañca vāre cha vā satta, parittajavanaṃ bhave;

Sakiṃ dve vā tadālambaṃ, sakimāvajjanādayo.

Five, six, or seven times the sense-sphere impulsion occurs; once or twice, registration; once, adverting and the others.

117.

117.

Appanājavanañcekaṃ, paṭhamuppattiyaṃ pana;

Tato paraṃ vasībhūtaṃ, ahorattaṃ pavattati.

In its first arising, the absorption-impulsion is a single moment; thereafter, having been mastered, it can continue for a day and a night.

118.

118.

Sakiṃ [M 0.0011] dve vā nirodhassa, samāpattikkhaṇe pana;

Catutthāruppajavanaṃ, tato cittaṃ nirujjhati.

At the moment of attaining cessation, the fourth immaterial impulsion occurs once or twice, then consciousness ceases.

119.

119.

Nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa, upariṭṭhaphaladvayaṃ;

Pañcābhiññā tathā maggā, ekacittakkhaṇā matā.

For one emerging from cessation, one of the two higher fruit-consciousnesses arises. The five higher knowledges and the paths are also considered to last for a single mind-moment.

120.

120.

Phalamekadvayaṃ tathā, tisso vā maggavīthiyaṃ;

Samāpattikkhaṇe tampi, ahorattaṃ pavattati.

Likewise, in a path-process, the fruit-consciousness occurs for one, two, or three moments. In the attainment of fruition, that too can continue for a day and a night.

121.

121.

Pañcadvāre na labbhanti, lokuttaramahaggatā;

Vīthimuttamanodhātu, pañca cittāni antime.

In the five sense doors, the supramundane and the sublime are not obtained. Process-freed [consciousness], the mind-element, and the five [sense-]consciousnesses are final.

122.

122.

Parittāneva sabbāni, pañcadvāresu sambhavā;

Manodvāramhi voṭṭhabba-tadālambajavā siyuṃ.

All [consciousnesses] arising at the five sense-doors are of the sense-sphere only; at the mind-door, there may be determining, registration, and impulsion.

123.

123.

Ghānajivhākāyavīthi, tadārammaṇameva ca;

Rūpe natthi tathārūpe, cakkhusotāpi vīthiyo.

The processes of smell, tongue, and body, and also registration, do not exist in the Form Realm; likewise, in the Formless Realm, eye and ear processes also do not exist.

124.

124.

Sabbāpi [V 0.0013] vīthiyo kāme,

Rūpe tisso pakāsitā;

Ekā vīthi panārūpe,

Natthāsaññīsu kācipi.

All cognitive processes are found in the sense-sphere; in the form-sphere, three are declared; one process, however, is in the formless-sphere; but none at all in the non-percipient realm.

125.

125.

Sattāpi vīthicittāni, kāme rūpe cha sambhavā;

Arūpe dve manodvārā-vajjanaṃ javananti cāti.

All seven process-consciousnesses arise in the sense-sphere; six arise in the form-sphere; in the formless-sphere, two – mind-door adverting and impulsion – arise.

Iti cittavibhāge vīthisaṅgahakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the discourse on the compendium of processes in the division of consciousness.

Tatiyo paricchedo.

The Third Chapter.

Catuttho paricchedo

The Fourth Chapter.

4. Vīthiparikammakathā

4. Discourse on the Preliminaries of the Cognitive Process.

126.

126.

Paṭhamāvajjanaṃ pañca-dasannaṃ parato bhave;

Dutiyāvajjanaṃ hoti, ekavīsatito paraṃ.

First adverting occurs after fifteen (consciousnesses); second adverting occurs after twenty-one.

127.

127.

Ekamhā [M 0.0012] pañcaviññāṇaṃ, pañcamhā sampaṭicchanaṃ;

Sukhasantīraṇaṃ hoti, pañcavīsatito paraṃ.

From one (consciousness) arise the five sense-consciousnesses; from the five (sense-consciousnesses) arises receiving consciousness; pleasant investigating consciousness occurs after twenty-five.

128.

128.

Sattatiṃsatito hoti, upekkhātīraṇadvayaṃ;

Voṭṭhabbanasarūpānaṃ, dvinnaṃ kāmajavā paraṃ.

After thirty-seven (consciousnesses) occur the two investigating consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity; after the two that have the nature of determining, the sense-sphere impulsions follow.

129.

129.

Maggābhiññā paraṃ dvinnaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ lokiyappanā;

Phalā catunnaṃ pañcannaṃ, upariṭṭhaphaladvayaṃ.

After two (types of consciousness), the path and higher knowledges arise; after three, mundane absorption arises; after four or five, the fruits arise, and the two higher fruits also arise.

130.

130.

Bhavanti cattālīsamhā, sukhapākā dvihetukā;

Tathekacattālīsamhā, upekkhāya samāyutā.

From forty (consciousnesses) arise the two-rooted resultant consciousnesses accompanied by happiness; similarly, from forty-one arise those associated with equanimity.

131.

131.

Honti [V 0.0014] sattatito kāme, sukhapākā tihetukā;

Dvāsattatimhā jāyanti, upekkhāsahitā pana.

In the sense-sphere, from seventy (consciousnesses) arise the three-rooted resultant consciousnesses accompanied by happiness; from seventy-two, however, arise those accompanied by equanimity.

132.

132.

Ekūnasaṭṭhito rūpa-pākā pākā arūpino;

Kamāṭṭhacattālīsamhā, tathekadvitihīnato.

From fifty-nine (consciousnesses) arise the form-sphere resultants; the formless-sphere resultants arise in order from forty-eight, and similarly from that number decreased by one, two, and three.

133.

133.

Pubbasaṅgahamiccevaṃ, vigaṇetvā vicakkhaṇo;

Parasaṅgahasaṅkhyādiṃ, vibhāveyya visārado.

Having thus reckoned the preceding collection, the discerning expert should skillfully make clear the numbers and so forth of the subsequent collection.

134.

134.

Pañcadvārāvajjanato, dasa cittāni dīpaye;

Sesāvajjanato pañcacattālīsanti bhāsitaṃ.

From the five-door adverting, ten consciousnesses should be shown; from the remaining adverting, it is said there are forty-five.

135.

135.

Pañcaviññāṇato pāpavipākā sampaṭicchanā;

Paramekaṃ dvayaṃ puññavipākā sampaṭicchanā.

From the five sense-consciousnesses arise the receiving consciousnesses of unwholesome result; after them, one or two receiving consciousnesses of wholesome result arise.

136.

136.

Santīraṇā dvihetumhā, pākā dvādasa jāyare;

Tihetukāmapākamhā, ekavīsati labbhare.

From the two-rooted investigating consciousness, twelve resultant consciousnesses are produced; from the three-rooted sense-sphere resultant consciousness, twenty-one are obtained.

137.

137.

Rūpāvacarapākamhā, paramekūnavīsati;

Navaṭṭhārūpapākamhā, satta chāpi yathākkamaṃ.

From the resultant form-sphere consciousness, nineteen are obtained; from the nine and eight resultant formless-sphere consciousnesses, seven and six respectively.

138.

138.

Paṭighamhā tu satteva, sitamhā teraseritā;

Pāpapuññadvihetumhā, ekavīsati bhāvaye.

From aversion, indeed just seven (consciousnesses arise); from laughter, thirteen are stated; from unwholesome and wholesome two-rooted (consciousnesses), twenty-one should be understood.

139.

139.

Dvihetukāmakriyato[M 0.0013], aṭṭhārasa upekkhakā;

Sattarasa sukhopetā, vibhāveyya vicakkhaṇo.

From two-rooted sense-sphere functional (consciousness), eighteen are accompanied by equanimity; seventeen are accompanied by happiness; the discerning one should distinguish them.

140.

140.

Kāmapuññatihetumhā, tettiṃseva upekkhakā;

Tepaññāsa sukhopetā, bhavantīti pakāsitaṃ.

From wholesome three-rooted sense-sphere (consciousness), thirty-three are accompanied by equanimity; fifty-three are accompanied by happiness, thus it is declared.

141.

141.

Tihetukāmakriyato, catuvīsatipekkhakā;

Sukhitamhā tu dīpeyya, pañcavīsati paṇḍito.

From three-rooted sense-sphere functional (consciousness), twenty-four are accompanied by equanimity; from that accompanied by happiness, the wise one should show twenty-five.

142.

142.

Dasarūpajavamhekā-dasadvādasa [V 0.0015] terasa;

Yathākkamaṃ pañcadasa, āruppā paridīpaye.

From the ten form-sphere impulsions, eleven, twelve, and thirteen (resultants arise); in order, from the formless ones, one should explain fifteen.

143.

143.

Phalamhā cuddasevāhu, maggamhā tu sakaṃ phalaṃ;

Paraṃ saṅgahamiccevaṃ, vigaṇeyya visārado.

From fruition, they say just fourteen (arise); from the path, however, its own fruit. Thus, the wise one should reckon the subsequent collection.

144.

144.

Pubbāparasamodhāna-miti ñatvā tato paraṃ;

Vatthuvīthisamodhānaṃ, yathāsambhavamuddise.

Having thus known the connection of what precedes and what follows, one should then indicate the connection of the bases and processes as is appropriate.

145.

145.

Pañca vatthūni nissāya, kamato pañcamānasā;

Tettiṃsa pana nissāya, hadayaṃ mānasā siyuṃ.

Depending on the five bases, in order, the five sense-consciousnesses arise; but thirty-three consciousnesses depend on the heart-base.

146.

146.

Kāmapākamanodhātu-hasituppādamānasā;

Dosamūlāni maggo ca, rūpajjhānāva sabbathā.

The sense-sphere resultant mind-element, the smile-producing consciousness, consciousnesses rooted in aversion, the path, and all the form jhānas.

147.

147.

Dasāvasesāpuññāni, kāmapuññamahākriyā;

Voṭṭhabbārūpajavanaṃ, satta lokuttarāni ca.

The remaining ten unwholesome consciousnesses, the great wholesome and functional sense-sphere consciousnesses, determining, formless-sphere impulsions, and the seven supramundane consciousnesses.

148.

148.

Dvecattālīsa cittāni, pañcavokārabhūmiyaṃ;

Nissāya hadayaṃ honti, arūpe nissayaṃ vinā.

Forty-two consciousnesses occur in the five-constituent plane; they depend on the heart-base, but in the formless-sphere, they are without dependence.

149.

149.

Āruppapākā cattāro, anissāyeti sabbathā;

Vitthārenaṭṭhadhā bhinnaṃ, saṅkhepā tividhaṃ bhave.

The four formless-sphere resultants are entirely without dependence; in detail, this is divided eightfold, in brief, it becomes threefold.

150.

150.

Tecattālīsa nissāya, anissāya catubbidhaṃ;

Nissitānissitā sesā, dvecattālīsa mānasā.

Forty-three are dependent, four are independent; the remaining forty-two minds are both dependent and independent.

151.

151.

Pañca cittappanā honti, kamenekekavīthiyaṃ;

Manodhātuttikaṃ nāma, pañcadvārikamīritaṃ.

Five impulsions occur, one by one in each process; the mind-element triad is said to arise in the five-door process.

152.

152.

Sukhatīraṇavoṭṭhabba-parittajavanā [M 0.0014] pana;

Ekatiṃsāpi jāyante, chasu vīthīsu sambhavā.

Joyful investigation, determining, and limited impulsions: these thirty-one also arise, being possible in the six processes.

153.

153.

Mahāpākā panaṭṭhāpi, upekkhātīraṇadvayaṃ;

Chasu dvāresu jāyanti, dasa muttā ca vīthiyā.

The eight great resultants and the two investigating-consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity arise in the six doors; and ten are free from process.

154.

154.

Cutisandhibhavaṅgānaṃ, vasā pākā mahaggatā;

Nava vīthivimuttāti, dasadhā vīthisaṅgaho.

The nine exalted resultants, by way of death, rebirth-linking, and life-continuum, are free from process; thus the summary of processes is tenfold.

155.

155.

Ekadvārikacittāni[V 0.0016], pañcachadvārikā tathā;

Chadvārikavimuttā ca, vimuttāti ca sabbathā.

There are consciousnesses of a single door, likewise of five and six doors; and those freed from the six doors, and those entirely freed.

156.

156.

Chattiṃsa tayekatiṃsa, dasa ceva naveti ca;

Ñatvā vīthisamodhānaṃ, gocarañca samuddise.

Thirty-six, thirty-one, ten, and also nine; having known the combination of processes, one should explain their objects.

157.

157.

Kamato pañcaviññāṇā, lokuttaramahaggatā;

Abhiññāvajjitā sabbā, pañcatālīsa mānasā.

Respectively, the five sense-consciousnesses, the supramundane, and the exalted—all these, excluding the higher knowledges—are forty-five minds.

158.

158.

Yathāsambhavato honti, rūpādekekagocarā;

Pañcagocaramīrenti, manodhātuttikaṃ pana.

According to their arising, they have a single object such as form; but the triad of mind-element traverses the five objects.

159.

159.

Santīraṇamahāpākā, parittajavanāni ca;

Voṭṭhabbanamabhiññā ca, tecattālīsa sambhavā.

Investigating-consciousnesses, great resultants, and limited impulsions, determining-consciousness and higher knowledges—these forty-three arise.

160.

160.

Chārammaṇesu hontīti, aṭṭhadhā tividhā puna;

Ekārammaṇacittāni, pañcachārammaṇāni ca.

They occur with six objects; again, the classification is eightfold and threefold. There are single-object consciousnesses, and those with five and six objects.

161.

161.

Saṅkhepā mānasā pañca-cattālīsa tayo tathā;

Tecattālīsa ceveti, sattadhāpi siyuṃ kathaṃ.

In summary, the minds are forty-five, likewise three, and also forty-three; how then can they also be sevenfold?

162.

162.

Kāmapākamanodhātu-hasituppādamānasā;

Pañcavīsa yathāyogaṃ, parittārammaṇā matā.

The sense-sphere resultants, the mind-element, and the smile-producing consciousness—these twenty-five, as appropriate, are considered to have a limited object.

163.

163.

Kasiṇugghāṭimākāsaṃ, paṭhamāruppamānasaṃ;

Tasseva natthibhāvaṃ tu, tatiyāruppakaṃ tathā.

The first formless-sphere mind has as its object the space from the removed kasiṇa; likewise, the third formless-sphere mind has as its object the non-existence of that very consciousness.

164.

164.

Ālambitvā pavattanti, āruppā kamato tato;

Dutiyañca catutthañca, cha mahaggatagocarā.

The second and the fourth formless attainments proceed in order, taking the preceding one as object; these six have an exalted consciousness as their object.

165.

165.

Appamāṇasamaññā [M 0.0015] te, nibbāne pana gocare;

Aṭṭha lokuttarā dhammā, niyamena vavatthitā.

The eight supramundane states, however, have Nibbāna as their object; they are fixed by necessity and are known as the 'unlimited'.

166.

166.

Kasiṇāsubhakoṭṭhāse,

Ānāpāne ca yogino;

Paṭibhāganimittamhi[V 0.0017],

Appamaññānuyuñjato.

For a yogi, in the counterpart sign arising from the kasiṇas, foulness, parts of the body, and mindfulness of breathing; and for one applying himself to the immeasurables,

167.

167.

Sattapaṇṇattiyañceva, rūpajjhānaṃ pavattati;

Yathāvuttanimittamhi, sesamāruppakanti ca.

On the concept of beings, the form-sphere jhānas occur; in the sign as described, the remaining are the formless-sphere consciousnesses.

168.

168.

Abhiññāvajjitā ekavīsa mahaggatā sabbā;

Sabbe paṇṇattisaṅkhāte, navattabbe pavattare.

All twenty-one exalted consciousnesses, excluding the higher knowledges, occur with an object termed 'concept'; they do not occur otherwise.

169.

169.

Jāyantākusalā ñāṇavippayuttajavā tathā;

Appamāṇaṃ vinā vīsa, parittādīsu tīsupi.

Unwholesome consciousnesses arise, and likewise knowledge-disconnected impulsions; these twenty, excluding the immeasurables, occur with the three kinds of objects beginning with the limited.

170.

170.

Tihetukāmapuññāni, puññābhiññā ca pañcime;

Catūsupi pavattanti, arahattadvayaṃ vinā.

The three-rooted sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses and the wholesome higher knowledge—these five occur with all four types of objects, except for the path and fruit of Arahantship.

171.

171.

Kriyābhiññā ca voṭṭhabbaṃ, kriyākāme tihetukā;

Cha sabbatthāpi hontīti, sattadhā mānasā ṭhitā.

The functional higher knowledge, the determining-consciousness, and the three-rooted functional sense-sphere consciousnesses—these six occur with all objects; thus the minds are established in a sevenfold way.

172.

172.

Ekaticcatukoṭṭhāsagocarā tividhā pana;

Samasaṭṭhi tathā vīsa, kamenekādaseti ca.

They are of three kinds, having objects belonging to one, three, or four categories: sixty, twenty, and eleven, respectively.

173.

173.

Pañcadvāresu pañcāpi, paccuppannāva gocarā;

Tekālikā navattabbā, manodvāre yathārahaṃ.

In the five doors, the five sense-consciousnesses have only the present as their object; in the mind-door, objects may be of the three times or timeless, as is appropriate.

174.

174.

Ajjhattā ca bahiddhā ca, pañcadvāresu gocarā;

Manodvāre navattabbo, natthibhāvopi labbhati.

Objects in the five doors are both internal and external; in the mind-door, timeless concepts and also non-existence are found as objects.

175.

175.

Pañcadvāresu pañcanna-mekameko ca gocaro;

Chāpi ārammaṇā honti, manodvāramhi sabbathā.

In the five doors, for each of the five, there is a single object; all six objects occur in the mind-door in every way.

176.

176.

Pañcadvāresu gahitaṃ, tadaññampi ca gocaraṃ;

Manodvāre vavatthānaṃ, gacchatīti hi desitaṃ.

It is taught that in the mind-door, determination proceeds regarding an object grasped through the five doors, or regarding another object.

177.

177.

Atītā [M 0.0016] vattamānā ca, sambhavā kāmasandhiyā;

Chadvāragahitā honti, tividhā tepi gocarā.

Past, present, and future objects, arising from the sense-sphere continuity, are grasped through the six doors; thus their objects are threefold.

178.

178.

Kammanimittamevekaṃ[V 0.0018], manodvāre upaṭṭhitaṃ;

Navattabbamatītañca, dhammārammaṇasaṅgahaṃ.

The kamma-sign alone, presented at the mind-door, being timeless or past, is included under the dhamma-object.

179.

179.

Ālambitvā yathāyogaṃ, paṭisandhimahaggatā;

Ante cuti bhave majjhe, bhavaṅgampi pavattatīti.

Taking that object as is appropriate, exalted rebirth-linking occurs; at the end of existence, death, and in the middle, the life-continuum also proceeds.

Iti cittavibhāge vīthiparikammakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the discourse on the preliminary work of thought-processes in the analysis of consciousness.

Catuttho paricchedo.

The Fourth Chapter.

Pañcamo paricchedo

The Fifth Chapter.

5. Bhūmipuggalakathā

5. The Discourse on Planes and Individuals.

180.

180.

Ito paraṃ pavakkhāmi, bhūmipuggalabhedato;

Cittānaṃ pana sabbesaṃ, kamato saṅgahaṃ kathaṃ.

Hereafter I shall explain the classification of all consciousnesses, in due order, according to planes and individuals.

181.

181.

Nirayañca tiracchānayoni petāsurā tathā;

Caturāpāyabhūmīti, kāme duggatiyo matā.

Hell, the animal realm, the realm of ghosts, and the asuras as well—these four realms of misery are considered woeful destinies within the sensual sphere.

182.

182.

Cātumahārājikā ca, tāvatiṃsā ca yāmakā;

Tusitā ceva nimmānaratino vasavattino.

The devas of the Four Great Kings, the Tāvatiṃsa, and the Yāma; the Tusita, the Nimmānaratī, and the Vasavattī.

183.

183.

Chaḷete devalokā ca, mānavāti ca sattadhā;

Kāmasugatiyo cekādasadhā kāmabhūmiyo.

These six are the deva worlds, and with the human world they are sevenfold; these are the sensual happy destinations. The sensual planes are eleven in all.

184.

184.

Brahmānaṃ pārisajjā ca, tathā brahmapurohitā;

Mahābrahmā ca tividhā, paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyo.

Brahmā's Retinue, Brahmā's Ministers, and the Great Brahmās—these three are the planes of the first jhāna.

185.

185.

Parittābhāppamāṇābhā, tathevābhassarāti ca;

Dutiyajjhānabhūmi ca, tividhāva pakāsitā.

The devas of Limited Radiance, the devas of Immeasurable Radiance, and likewise the devas of Streaming Radiance—the plane of the second jhāna is thus declared to be threefold.

186.

186.

Parittasubhāppamāṇāsubhā ca subhakiṇhakā;

Tividhāpi pavuccanti, tatiyajjhānabhūmiyo.

The devas of Limited Glory, the devas of Immeasurable Glory, and the devas of Refulgent Glory—these three are also called the planes of the third jhāna.

187.

187.

Vehapphalā [M 0.0017][V 0.0019] asaññī ca, suddhāvāsā ca pañcadhā;

Iccetā pana sattāpi, catutthajjhānabhūmiyo.

The Great-Fruited devas, the non-percipient beings, and the five Pure Abodes—these seven, then, are the planes of the fourth jhāna.

188.

188.

Avihā ca atappā ca, sudassā ca sudassino;

Akaniṭṭhāti pañcete, suddhāvāsā pakāsitā.

The Aviha, the Atappa, the Sudassa, the Sudassī, and the Akaniṭṭha—these five are declared to be the Pure Abodes.

189.

189.

Iti soḷasadhā bhinnā, brahmalokā pavuccare;

Rūpibrahmānamāvāsā, rūpāvacarabhūmiyo.

Thus the Brahmā worlds are said to be sixteenfold; they are the abodes of the fine-material Brahmās, the planes of the fine-material sphere.

190.

190.

Ākāsānañcāyatananāmādīhi pakāsitā;

Arūpibrahmalokā ca, catudhārūpabhūmiyo.

The immaterial Brahmā worlds, designated by names beginning with 'the base of infinite space,' are the four immaterial planes.

191.

191.

Sotāpannādibhedena, catudhānuttarā matā;

Pañcatiṃsa paniccevaṃ, sabbathāpi ca bhūmiyo.

The supramundane is considered fourfold, distinguished as the stream-enterer and so on; thus in all there are thirty-five planes.

192.

192.

Jāyanti caturāpāye, pāpapākāya sandhiyā;

Kāmāvacaradevesu, mahāpākehi jāyare.

Through rebirth-linking by the result of evil, one is born in the four woeful planes; by great resultants, one is born among the devas of the sensual sphere.

193.

193.

Ahetukā puññapākāhetukena tu jāyare;

Bhummadevamanussesu, mahāpākehi cetare.

However, rootless individuals are born by means of a rootless meritorious resultant; among terrestrial devas and humans, others are born by the great resultants.

194.

194.

Vipākaṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ, paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ;

Dutiyaṃ tatiyañceva, dutiyajjhānabhūmiyaṃ.

The result of the first jhāna is rebirth in the first jhāna plane; the second and third jhānas lead to rebirth in the second jhāna plane.

195.

195.

Tatiyamhi catutthaṃ tu, catutthamhi ca pañcamaṃ;

Āruppā ca kameneva, āruppe honti sandhiyo.

The fourth jhāna leads to the third jhāna plane, and the fifth jhāna to the fourth jhāna plane; and the immaterial attainments, in sequence, lead to rebirth-linking in the immaterial realms.

196.

196.

Kāyavācāmanodvāre, kammaṃ pāṇavadhādikaṃ;

Katvā pāpakacittehi, jāyantāpāyabhūmiyaṃ.

Having committed deeds such as killing living beings through the doors of body, speech, and mind with unwholesome states of consciousness, one is reborn in the woeful planes.

197.

197.

Kāyavācāmanodvāre, dānaṃ sīlañca bhāvanaṃ;

Kāmapuññehi katvāna, kāmasugatiyaṃ siyuṃ.

Having performed sensual-sphere meritorious deeds such as giving, virtue, and mental development through the doors of body, speech, and mind, one is reborn in a sensual happy destination.

198.

198.

Parittaṃ majjhimaṃ jhānaṃ, paṇītañca yathākkamaṃ;

Bhāvetvā tividhā honti, tīsu bhūmīsu yogino.

Having developed the jhāna as inferior, medium, or superior, yogis are reborn accordingly in the three planes of the first jhāna.

199.

199.

Vehapphalesu [V 0.0020] jāyanti, bhāvetvā pañcamaṃ tathā;

Saññāvirāgatañceva, bhāvetvāsaññibhūmiyaṃ.

By developing the fifth jhāna, they are reborn among the Great-Fruited devas; and by developing dispassion towards perception, they are reborn in the plane of non-percipient beings.

200.

200.

Suddhāvāsesu [M 0.0018] jāyanti, anāgāmikapuggalā;

Āruppāni ca bhāvetvā, arūpesu yathākkamaṃ.

Non-returners are reborn in the Pure Abodes; and having developed the immaterial attainments, they are reborn in the immaterial realms in sequential order.

201.

201.

Lokuttaraṃ tu bhāvetvā, yathāsakamanantaraṃ;

Samāpattikkhaṇe ceva, appeti phalamānasaṃ.

But having developed a supramundane path, immediately following the moment of its attainment, the corresponding fruit-consciousness arises.

202.

202.

Apāyamhā cutā sattā, kāmadhātumhi jāyare;

Sabbaṭṭhānesu jāyanti, kāmasugatito cutā.

Beings who pass away from a woeful plane are reborn in the sensual sphere; those who pass away from a sensual happy destination may be reborn in any plane.

203.

203.

Cutā jāyanti rūpamhā, sabbatthāpāyavajjite;

Kāmasugatiyaṃ honti, arūpāsaññato cutā.

Those who pass away from the fine-material sphere are reborn anywhere except in the woeful planes. Those who pass away from the immaterial sphere or the non-percipient plane are reborn in a sensual happy destination.

204.

204.

Tathārūpacutā honti, tatthevoparimeva ca;

Vaṭṭamūlasamucchedā, nibbāyanti anāsavā.

Those who pass away from such a fine-material realm are reborn either in that same realm or in a higher one. Having eradicated the root of the round of existence, the taintless ones attain final Nibbāna.

205.

205.

Suddhāvāsesvanāgāmi-puggalāvopapajjare;

Kāmadhātumhi jāyanti, anāgāmivivajjitā.

Only non-returners are reborn in the Pure Abodes; those who are not non-returners are born in the sensual sphere.

206.

206.

Heṭṭhupapattibrahmānaṃ, ariyānaṃ na katthaci;

Asaññasattāpāyesu, natthevāriyapuggalā.

Noble ones are never reborn in a lower Brahmā world. Moreover, noble individuals do not exist in the plane of non-percipient beings or in the woeful planes.

207.

207.

Vehapphale akaniṭṭhe, bhavagge ca patiṭṭhitā;

Na punāññattha jāyanti, sabbe ariyapuggalā.

Established in the Great-Fruited plane, the Akaniṭṭha plane, and at the peak of existence, all noble individuals are not reborn elsewhere.

208.

208.

Chasu devesvanāgāmī, vītarāgā na tiṭṭhare;

Na ciraṭṭhāyino tattha, lokiyāpi ca yogino.

Being free from sensual lust, non-returners do not remain in the six deva worlds. Worldly yogis, too, do not remain there long.

209.

209.

Gihiliṅge na tiṭṭhanti, manussesu anāsavā;

Pabbajjāyañca bhumme ca, brahmattepi ca tiṭṭhare.

Taintless ones do not remain in the lay life among humans; they remain in the state of homelessness, among the terrestrial devas, and in the sublime state of a Brahmā.

210.

210.

Yāni paññāsa vassāni,

Manussānaṃ sa piṇḍito;

Eko [V 0.0021] rattidivo tena,

Māseko tiṃsa rattiyo.

What for humans is fifty years, taken together, is a single day and night for them. A month for them consists of thirty such days.

211.

211.

Dvādasamāsiyo vasso, tena pañcasataṃ bhave;

Cātumahārājikānaṃ, pamāṇamidamāyuno.

A year has twelve such months, and their lifespan is five hundred such years. This is the measure of the lifespan for the devas of the Four Great Kings.

212.

212.

Taṃ [M 0.0019] navutivassasata-sahassaṃ pana piṇḍitaṃ;

Gaṇanāya manussānaṃ, catubhāgūparūpari.

Calculated in human years, that lifespan amounts to nine million years. From here on up, the lifespan quadruples for each subsequent realm.

213.

213.

Yaṃ manussavassasataṃ, tadeko divaso kato;

Tena vassasahassāyu, tāvatiṃsesu desito.

What is a hundred human years is a single day for them; thus a lifespan of a thousand such years is taught for the Tāvatiṃsa devas.

214.

214.

Koṭittayaṃ saṭṭhisatasahassañcādhikaṃ bhave;

Gaṇanāya manussānaṃ, tāvatiṃsesu piṇḍitaṃ.

Calculated in human years, the total for the Tāvatiṃsa devas comes to thirty-six million years.

215.

215.

Āyuppamāṇamiccevaṃ, devānamuparūpari;

Dvikkhattuṃ dviguṇaṃ katvā, catubhāgamudāhaṭaṃ.

Thus is the measure of life for the devas in the realms higher and higher: for each realm, the lifespan is quadrupled.

216.

216.

Gaṇanāya manussānaṃ, tattha cuddasa koṭiyo;

Cattālīsasatasahassādhikā yāmabhūmiyaṃ.

Calculated in human years, the lifespan in the Yāma plane is one hundred forty-four million years.

217.

217.

Tusitānaṃ pakāsenti, sattapaññāsa koṭiyo;

Saṭṭhisatasahassāni, vassāni adhikāni ca.

For the Tusita devas, they declare a lifespan of five hundred seventy-six million years.

218.

218.

Nimmānaratidevānaṃ, dvisataṃ tiṃsa koṭiyo;

Cattālīsavassasatasahassāni ca sabbathā.

For the Nimmānaratī devas, the lifespan is in all two billion, three hundred four million years.

219.

219.

Navakoṭisatañcekavīsativassakoṭiyo;

Saṭṭhivassasatasahassādhikā vasavattisu.

In the Vasavattī realm, the lifespan is nine billion, two hundred sixteen million years.

220.

220.

Kappassa tatiyo bhāgo, upaḍḍhañca yathākkamaṃ;

Kappeko dve ca cattāro, aṭṭha kappā ca soḷasa.

A third of an aeon and a half of an aeon, respectively; then one aeon, two, four, eight, and sixteen aeons.

221.

221.

Dvattiṃsa catusaṭṭhī ca, navasu brahmabhūmisu;

Vehapphalā asaññī ca, pañcakappasatāyukā.

Thirty-two and sixty-four aeons are also among the lifespans in the nine Brahmā planes. The Great-Fruited devas and the non-percipient beings have a lifespan of five hundred aeons.

222.

222.

Kappasahassaṃ [V 0.0022] dve cattāri, aṭṭha soḷasa cakkamā;

Sahassāni ca kappānaṃ, suddhāvāsānamuddise.

One thousand, two thousand, four thousand, eight thousand, and sixteen thousand aeons in succession are assigned to the Pure Abodes.

223.

223.

Vīsakappasahassāni, cattālīsañca saṭṭhi ca;

Caturāsītisahassā, kappā cāruppake kamā.

Twenty thousand, forty thousand, sixty thousand, and eighty-four thousand aeons are assigned in succession to the formless planes.

224.

224.

Āyuppamāṇaniyamo, natthi bhumme ca mānave;

Vassānaṃ gaṇanā natthi, caturāpāyabhūmiyaṃ.

There is no fixed measure of lifespan among the terrestrial devas and human beings; there is no counting of years in the four woeful planes.

225.

225.

Puthujjanāriyā [M 0.0020] ceti, duvidhā honti puggalā;

Tihetukādibhedena, tividhā ca puthujjanā.

Worldlings and noble ones—these are the two kinds of individuals; and worldlings are of three kinds, distinguished by being rootless, two-rooted, or three-rooted.

226.

226.

Maggaṭṭhā ca phalaṭṭhā ca,

Aṭṭhevāriyapuggalā;

Ādito satta sekkhā ca,

Asekkho cārahāparo.

Those established in the path and those established in the fruit are the eight noble individuals. The first seven are trainees, and the other is the non-trainee, the arahant.

227.

227.

Ahetukāva labbhanti, sattā duggatiyaṃ pana;

Tihetukāva labbhanti, rūpārūpe sacittakā.

However, in the woeful destination only rootless beings are found; in the form and formless realms with consciousness, only three-rooted beings are found.

228.

228.

Kāmāvacaradevesu, ahetukavivajjitā;

Vinipātāsure ceva, mānave ca tayopi ca.

Among the sense-sphere devas, individuals are found excluding the rootless type; among the fallen asuras and human beings, all three types are found.

229.

229.

Ariyā nāma labbhanti, asaññāpāyavajjite;

Puthujjanā tu labbhanti, suddhāvāsavivajjite.

Noble ones are found in all planes except the non-percipient plane and the woeful planes; but worldlings are found in all planes except the Pure Abodes.

230.

230.

Suddhāvāsamapāyañca, hitvāsaññibhavaṃ tidhā;

Sotāpannādayo dvepi, sesaṭṭhānesu labbhare.

Having excluded the three kinds of planes—the Pure Abodes, the woeful planes, and the non-percipient existence—the two, the stream-enterer and the once-returner, are found in the remaining places.

231.

231.

Iti sabbappabhedena, bhūmipuggalasaṅgahaṃ;

Ñatvā viññū vibhāveyya, tattha cittāni sambhavāti.

Thus, having understood this summary of planes and individuals in all its varieties, the wise person should analyze the consciousnesses that can arise in them.

Iti cittavibhāge bhūmipuggalakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the discourse on planes and individuals in the Division on Consciousness.

Pañcamo paricchedo.

The Fifth Chapter.

Chaṭṭho paricchedo

The Sixth Chapter

6. Bhūmipuggalacittappavattikathā

6. The Discourse on the Occurrence of Consciousness in Relation to Planes and Individuals

232.

232.

Kāmasugatiyaṃ [V 0.0023] honti, mahāpākā yathārahaṃ;

Mahaggatavipākā ca, yathāsandhivavatthitā.

In the sense-sphere happy destinations, great resultants occur as is appropriate; and exalted resultants are established according to the rebirth-linking.

233.

233.

Voṭṭhabbakāmapuññāni, viyuttāni ca diṭṭhiyā;

Uddhaccasahitañceti, honti sabbattha cuddasa.

Determining consciousness, sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, those dissociated from wrong view, and the one accompanied by restlessness—these fourteen occur everywhere.

234.

234.

Santīraṇamanodhātu-cakkhusotamanā [M 0.0021] pana;

Dasa cittāni jāyanti, sabbatthārūpavajjite.

Investigating consciousnesses, the mind-element, eye-consciousness, and ear-consciousness; these ten consciousnesses, for their part, arise everywhere except in the formless realm.

235.

235.

Diṭṭhigatasampayuttā, vicikicchāyutā tathā;

Pañca sabbattha jāyanti, suddhāvāsavivajjite.

The consciousnesses associated with wrong view and the one associated with doubt—these five arise everywhere except in the Pure Abodes.

236.

236.

Dosamūladvayañceva, ghānādittayamānasā;

Aṭṭha sabbattha jāyanti, mahaggatavivajjite.

The pair of consciousnesses rooted in hatred and the three pairs of sense consciousness beginning with nose-consciousness; these eight arise everywhere except in the exalted planes.

237.

237.

Catutthāruppajavanaṃ, anāgāmiphalādayo;

Mahākriyā ca jāyanti, terasāpāyavajjite.

The javanas of the fourth formless attainment, the fruit of the non-returner and the subsequent path and fruit, and the great functional consciousnesses—these thirteen arise, excluding the woeful planes.

238.

238.

Heṭṭhāruppajavā dve dve, chāpāyuparivajjite;

Sitarūpajavā honti, arūpāpāyavajjite.

The six lower formless javanas arise, excluding the woeful and form planes; the remaining form javanas arise, excluding the formless and woeful planes.

239.

239.

Sotāpattiphalādīni, suddhāpāyavivajjite;

Paṭhamānuttaraṃ suddhā-pāyārūpavivajjite.

The fruit of stream-entry and the subsequent attainments up to the path of non-returning arise, excluding the Pure Abodes and the woeful planes; the first supramundane consciousness arises, excluding the Pure Abodes, the woeful planes, and the formless planes.

240.

240.

Avatthābhūmibhūtattā, na gayhanti anuttarā;

Ekavokārabhūmi ca, rūpamattā na gayhati.

Because they are states, not planes of existence, the supramundane consciousnesses are not included; and the one-constituent plane, being merely matter, is also not included.

241.

241.

Sabhummā sabbabhummā ca, ekadvittayavajjitā;

Tathārūpasuddhāvāsa-brahmāpāyavasāti ca.

Consciousnesses are found in specific planes or in all planes, excluding one, two, or three types of planes; likewise for those dwelling in the form realm, the Pure Abodes, the Brahma worlds, and the woeful planes.

242.

242.

Mānasā [V 0.0024] pañca koṭṭhāsā, sattarasa catuddasa;

Chattiṃsatekavīsā ca, ekañceva yathākkamaṃ.

Consciousnesses are in five groups, numbering seventeen, fourteen, thirty-six, twenty-one, and one, respectively.

243.

243.

Aṭṭhārasāpi hontete, navadhāpi punekadhā;

Catudhā tividhā ceva, ekadhāti ca bhedato.

By way of division, these are also eighteenfold, ninefold, and single; and again fourfold, threefold, and single.

244.

244.

Terasāpi ca koṭṭhāsā, bhavantekatibhūmakā;

Chasattekādasasatta-rasabhūmakamānasā.

There are also thirteen groups of consciousnesses that are found in one to three planes; there are consciousnesses found in six, seven, eleven, and seventeen planes.

245.

245.

Ekadvayaticatukkapañcakādhikavīsajā;

Chabbīsatiṃsajā ceti, yathānukkamato bhave.

In order, there are consciousnesses found in twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-four, twenty-five, twenty-six, and thirty planes.

246.

246.

Cattāri puna cattāri, ekamaṭṭhaṭṭha cekakaṃ;

Cattārekādasa dve dve, satta tevīsa cuddasa.

Again four, four, one, eight, eight, and one; four, eleven, two, two, seven, twenty-three, fourteen.

247.

247.

Kriyājavamahāpākā[M 0.0022], lokuttaramahaggatā;

Dvepaññāsa na labbhanti, caturāpāyabhūmiyaṃ.

Functional javanas, great resultants, supramundane and exalted consciousnesses—these fifty-two are not found in the four woeful planes.

248.

248.

Kāmāvacaradevesu, chasu bhumme ca mānave;

Kāmasugatiyaṃ natthi, nava pākā mahaggatā.

In the sense-sphere happy destinations—the six deva planes and the human plane—the nine exalted resultant consciousnesses are not found.

249.

249.

Dosamūlamahāpākā, ghānādittayamānasā;

Natthārūpavipākā ca, vīsatī rūpabhūmiyaṃ.

The two consciousnesses rooted in hatred, the eight great resultants, the three pairs of sense consciousness beginning with the nose, and the formless resultants—these twenty are not found in the form realm.

250.

250.

Kaṅkhādiṭṭhiyutā pañcārūpapākā catubbidhā;

Pañcādonuttarā ceva, suddhāvāse na labbhare.

The five consciousnesses connected with doubt and wrong view, the four kinds of formless resultants, the five form-sphere resultants, and the first four supramundane consciousnesses are not found in the Pure Abodes.

251.

251.

Ādāvajjanamaggā ca, paṭighārūpamānasā;

Kāmapākā sitārūpe, tecattālīsa natthi te.

Adverting consciousnesses, the first path, aversion, form-sphere consciousnesses, and sense-sphere resultants—these forty-three are not found in the formless realm.

252.

252.

Sattatiṃsa parittā ca, labbhantāpāyabhūmiyaṃ;

Mānasāsīti labbhanti, kāmasugatiyaṃ pana.

Thirty-seven sense-sphere consciousnesses are found in the woeful planes; but eighty consciousnesses are found in the sense-sphere happy destinations.

253.

253.

Ekūnasattati rūpe, suddhe paññāsa pañca ca;

Chacattālīsa āruppe, natthāsaññīsu kiñcipi.

Sixty-nine types of consciousness are found in the form realm, fifty-five in the Pure Abodes, and forty-six in the formless realm; in the non-percipient plane, there is nothing at all.

254.

254.

Itthamekadviticatupañcabhummāni [V 0.0025] soḷasa;

Dasa pañcadasevātha, catuttiṃsa catuddasa.

Thus consciousnesses are found in one, two, three, four, five, and sixteen planes; then in ten, fifteen, thirty-four, and fourteen planes.

255.

255.

Apāyāhetukānaṃ tu, mahāpākakriyājave;

Hitvā sesaparittāni, cittāni pana labbhare.

For rootless beings of the woeful planes, however, excluding the great resultants, functional consciousnesses, and javanas, the remaining sense-sphere consciousnesses are found.

256.

256.

Dvihetukāhetukānaṃ, sesānaṃ kāmamānasā;

Labbhanti pana hitvāna, ñāṇapākakriyājave.

For the remaining two-rooted and rootless beings, sense-sphere consciousnesses are found, but excluding those associated with knowledge, namely, resultants, functional consciousnesses, and javanas.

257.

257.

Tihetukānaṃ sattānaṃ, tattha tatthūpapattiyaṃ;

Tattha tatthūpapannānaṃ, labbhamānāni labbhare.

For three-rooted beings, according to their particular rebirth, whatever consciousnesses are attainable by those reborn in such a state, those are found.

258.

258.

Tihetukānaṃ sabbepi, mānasāpāyapāṇinaṃ;

Sattatiṃsāvasesānaṃ, ekatālīsa niddise.

For three-rooted beings, all consciousnesses are possible. For beings in the woeful planes, there are thirty-seven. For the remaining beings, forty-one are to be specified.

259.

259.

Puthujjanāna sekkhānaṃ, na santi javanakriyā;

Na santi vītarāgānaṃ, puññāpuññāni sabbathā.

For worldlings and trainees, functional impulsions do not exist; for those free from passion, there is no merit and demerit whatsoever.

260.

260.

Kaṅkhādiṭṭhiyutā [M 0.0023] pañca, sekkhānaṃ natthi mānasā;

Dosamūladvayañcāpi, natthānāgāmino pana.

The five consciousnesses associated with doubt and wrong view do not occur for trainees; and for the non-returner, the two rooted in hatred also do not occur.

261.

261.

Vavatthitāriyesveva, yathāsakamanuttarā;

Maggaṭṭhānaṃ sako maggo, natthaññaṃ kiñci sabbathā.

For the established noble ones, the respective supramundane consciousnesses arise. For one attaining the path, only their own path-consciousness arises, and nothing else at all.

262.

262.

Puthujjanānaṃ dvinnampi, phalaṭṭhānaṃ yathākkamaṃ;

Tatiyassa phalaṭṭhassa, catutthassa ca sambhavā.

For worldlings, for the first two fruit-attainers respectively, for the third fruit-attainer, and for the fourth, the possible arisings are:

263.

263.

Tesaṭṭhi ceva cittāni, labbhantekūnasaṭṭhi ca;

Sattapaññāsa cittāni, tepaññāsa ca sabbathā.

Sixty-three consciousnesses indeed, and fifty-nine are obtained; fifty-seven consciousnesses, and fifty-three in all.

264.

264.

Catupaññāsa paññāsa, paññāsadvayahīnakā;

Kāmesu tesaṃ sambhonti, catutālīsa cakkamā.

Fifty-four, fifty, forty-eight, and forty-four respectively arise for them in the sense-sphere.

265.

265.

Tecattālīsa cekūnacattālīsa yathākkamaṃ;

Bhavantekūnatālīsa, pañcattiṃsa ca rūpisu.

Forty-three and thirty-nine respectively; thirty-nine and thirty-five arise in the fine-material sphere.

266.

266.

Sattavīsa [V 0.0026] ca tevīsa, tevīsa ca yathākkamaṃ;

Āruppesupi labbhanti, tesamaṭṭhāraseva ca.

Twenty-seven, twenty-three, and twenty-three respectively, and also eighteen, are obtained for them in the immaterial sphere.

267.

267.

Puthujjanā ca cattāro, apāyāhetukādayo;

Ariyā ceva aṭṭhāti, dvādasannaṃ vasā siyuṃ.

The worldlings are four—those in the woeful planes, the rootless ones, and so on; and the noble ones are eight. Thus there are twelve types of individuals.

268.

268.

Chabbidhā cittakoṭṭhāsā, ekapuggalikā tathā;

Catupañcachasattaṭṭha-puggalaṭṭhāti cakkamā.

There are six kinds of groups of consciousnesses, as well as those belonging to a single individual, and respectively to four, five, six, seven, and eight individuals.

269.

269.

Chabbīsa cuddasevātha, terasa dve ca mānasā;

Dasa sattādhikā ceva, puna sattādhikā dasāti.

Twenty-six, then fourteen, thirteen, and two consciousnesses; then seventeen, and again seventeen.

Iti cittavibhāge bhūmipuggalacittappavattikathā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the discussion on the occurrence of consciousness according to plane and individual in the Analysis of Consciousness.

Chaṭṭho paricchedo.

The Sixth Chapter.

Sattamo paricchedo

The Seventh Chapter.

7. Bhūmipuggalasambhavakathā

7. The Discussion on Arising according to Plane and Individual

270.

270.

Dvihetukāhetukānaṃ[M 0.0024], na sampajjati appanā;

Arahattañca natthīti, nattheva javanakriyā.

For two-rooted and rootless individuals, absorption is not attained; and since Arahantship is not possible for them, there are no functional impulsions.

271.

271.

Ñāṇapākā na vattanti, jaḷattā mūlasandhiyā;

Dvihetukatadālambaṃ, siyā sugatiyaṃ na vā.

Resultant consciousness accompanied by knowledge does not occur, due to the weakness of the root-connection. The two-rooted registration consciousness may or may not arise in a happy-destiny being.

272.

272.

Tihetukānaṃ sattānaṃ, samathañca vipassanaṃ;

Bhāventānaṃ pavattanti, chabbīsatipi appanā.

For three-rooted beings who are developing serenity and insight, the twenty-six absorption consciousnesses arise.

273.

273.

Arahantāna sattānaṃ, bhavanti javanakriyā;

Yathābhūminiyāmena, ñāṇapākā ca labbhare.

For Arahant beings, functional impulsions occur; and according to the principle of their plane, resultants accompanied by knowledge are obtained.

274.

274.

Vajjhā [V 0.0027] paṭhamamaggena, kaṅkhādiṭṭhiyutā pana;

Paṭighaṃ tatiyeneva, kammamantena sāsavaṃ.

Those consciousnesses associated with doubt and wrong view are to be abandoned by the first path; aversion, by the third path alone; and by the final path, the remaining taints.

275.

275.

Tasmā tesaṃ na vattanti, tāni cittāni sabbathā;

Maggaṭṭhānaṃ tu maggova, nāññaṃ sambhoti kiñcipi.

Therefore, those consciousnesses do not occur for them at all. But for one attaining the path, only the path-consciousness arises; nothing else whatsoever arises.

276.

276.

Ahetukavipākāni, labbhamānāya vīthiyā;

Sabbathāpi ca sabbesaṃ, sambhavanti yathārahaṃ.

Rootless resultant consciousnesses, in any cognitive process that occurs, arise for all beings in every way, as is appropriate.

277.

277.

Pañcadvāre manodvāre, dhuvamāvajjanadvayaṃ;

Parittapuññāpuññāni, labbhanti lahuvuttito.

At the five doors and the mind door, the two advertings are constant; minor meritorious and demeritorious consciousnesses are obtained, owing to their swift activity.

278.

278.

Kriyājavanamappanā, natthāpāyesu kāraṇaṃ;

Natthi sahetukā pākā, duggatattā hi sandhiyā.

Functional impulsions and absorptions do not arise in the woeful planes; for, due to the woeful nature of the rebirth-linking, there are no rooted resultant consciousnesses.

279.

279.

Brahmānaṃ paṭighaṃ natthi, jhānavikkhambhitaṃ tathā;

Heṭṭhājhānaṃ virattattā, na bhāventi arūpino.

For Brahmās there is no aversion, as it is suppressed by jhāna; being detached from the lower jhānas, immaterial-sphere beings do not develop them.

280.

280.

Pubbeva diṭṭhasaccāva, ariyārūpabhūmakā;

Tasmādimaggo natthettha, kāyābhāvā sitaṃ tathā.

Noble beings in the immaterial planes have already seen the truths before; therefore the initial path does not arise there. Similarly, due to the absence of a physical body, the smiling consciousness does not arise.

281.

281.

Suddhāvāsāpi pattāva, heṭṭhānuttarapañcakaṃ;

Sattapāpapahīnā ca, tasmā natthettha tāni ca.

Those in the Pure Abodes have already attained the five lower supramundane consciousnesses and have abandoned the seven unwholesome consciousnesses; therefore these do not arise there.

282.

282.

Pañcadvārikacittāni[M 0.0025], dvārābhāve na vijjare;

Sahetukavipākā ca, yathābhūmivavatthitā.

Consciousnesses of the five doors do not exist in the absence of those doors; and rooted resultant consciousnesses are established according to their respective planes.

283.

283.

Sambhavāsambhavañcevaṃ, ñatvā puggalabhūmisu;

Labbhamānavasā tattha, cittasaṅgahamuddise.

Having thus known the possible and impossible arisings of consciousness in the classifications by individual and plane, one should explain the summary of consciousness there according to what is obtainable.

284.

284.

Kusalādippabhedā ca, tathā bhūmādibhedato;

Vatthudvārārammaṇato, bhūmipuggalatopi ca.

And the distinctions such as wholesome, and likewise the distinctions by plane and so on; by physical basis, door, and object; and also by plane and individual.

285.

285.

Vibhāgo yo samuddiṭṭho,

Cittānañca tu sambhavā;

Ñeyyo [V 0.0028] cetasikānañca,

Sampayogānusāratoti.

The analysis that has been set forth concerning consciousnesses and their arising should be understood to apply also to the mental factors, in accordance with their association.

Iti cittavibhāge bhūmipuggalasambhavakathā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the discussion on the arising according to plane and individual in the Analysis of Consciousness.

Sattamo paricchedo.

The Seventh Chapter.

Niṭṭhito ca cittavibhāgo.

The Analysis of Consciousness is concluded.

Aṭṭhamo paricchedo

The Eighth Chapter

2. Cetasikavibhāgo

2. The Analysis of Mental Factors

8. Cetasikasampayogakathā

8. The Discussion on the Association of Mental Factors

286.

286.

Iti cittavidhiṃ ñatvā, dvepaññāsa vibhāvinā;

Ñeyyā cetasi sambhūtā, dhammā cetasikā kathaṃ.

Having thus known the classification of consciousness, the wise should understand how the fifty-two phenomena that arise in consciousness, called mental factors, are to be known.

287.

287.

Phasso ca vedanā saññā, cetanekaggatā tathā;

Jīvitaṃ manasikāro, satta sādhāraṇā ime.

Contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, life-faculty, and attention—these seven are universals.

288.

288.

Vitakko ca vicāro ca, pīti ca vīriyaṃ tathā;

Chando ca adhimokkho ca, cha pakiṇṇakanāmakā.

Initial application, sustained application, rapture, energy, desire, and decision—these six are called the miscellaneous factors.

289.

289.

Puññāpuññesu pākesu, kriyāsu ca yathārahaṃ;

Mānasesu pavattanti, vippakiṇṇā pakiṇṇakā.

The miscellaneous factors arise scattered, as is appropriate, in wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional consciousness.

290.

290.

Saddhā [M 0.0026] satindriyañceva, hirottappabaladvayaṃ;

Alobho ca adoso ca, paññā majjhattatāpi ca.

Faith, mindfulness, moral shame, moral dread, non-greed, non-hatred, wisdom, and neutrality of mind.

291.

291.

Aṭṭhete [V 0.0029] uttamā nāma, dhammā uttamasādhanā;

Nivajjāti pavuccanti, yugaḷā cha tatopare.

These eight phenomena are called supreme, the means for supreme attainment; they are said to be blameless, and after them come six pairs.

292.

292.

Passaddhi kāyacittānaṃ, lahutā mudutā tathā;

Kammaññatā ca pāguñña-tā ca ujukatāti ca.

Tranquility of mental factors and of consciousness, likewise lightness, malleability, wieldiness, proficiency, and rectitude.

293.

293.

Appamaññādvayaṃ nāma, karuṇāmuditā siyuṃ;

Sammāvācā ca kammantā-jīvā ca viratittayaṃ.

The two illimitables, namely, compassion and altruistic joy; and the three abstinences: Right Speech, Right Action, and Right Livelihood.

294.

294.

Pañcavīsa paniccete, anavajjā yathārahaṃ;

Pāpāhetukamuttesu, anavajjesu jāyare.

These twenty-five factors are blameless. They arise, as is appropriate, in blameless consciousness, which is other than the unwholesome and rootless types.

295.

295.

Lobho doso ca moho ca,

Māno diṭṭhi ca saṃsayo;

Thinamiddhañca uddhaccaṃ,

Kukkuccañca tathā dasa.

Greed, hatred, and delusion; conceit, wrong view, and doubt; sloth, torpor, restlessness, and worry—thus ten.

296.

296.

Ahirīkamanottappaṃ, issā macchariyanti ca;

Honti cuddasa sāvajjā, sāvajjesveva sambhavā.

Shamelessness and lack of moral dread, envy, and avarice; these fourteen are blameworthy, arising only in blameworthy consciousness.

297.

297.

Dvepaññāsa catuddhevaṃ, dhammā cetasikā ṭhitā;

Tesaṃ dāni pavakkhāmi, sampayogañca saṅgahaṃ.

Thus the fifty-two mental factors are established in four groups. Now I shall explain their association and combination.

298.

298.

Satta sādhāraṇā sabba-cittasādhāraṇā tato;

Cittena saddhi aṭṭhannaṃ, vippayogo na katthaci.

The seven universals are common to all consciousness. Therefore, these eight—consciousness and its seven concomitants—are never dissociated from one another anywhere.

299.

299.

Vitakko pañcaviññāṇaṃ, dutiyādivivajjite;

Vicāropi ca tattheva, tatiyādivivajjite.

Initial application is excluded from the ten sense-consciousnesses and from the second jhana onwards. Sustained application is also excluded from the same, and from the third jhana onwards.

300.

300.

Somanassayute pīti-catutthajjhānavajjite;

Vīriyaṃ paṭhamāvajja-vipākāhetuvajjite.

Rapture is associated with consciousness accompanied by joy, but is excluded from the fourth jhana. Energy is excluded from the five-door adverting consciousness, the ten sense-consciousnesses, the two receiving consciousnesses, and the three investigating consciousnesses.

301.

301.

Chando sambhoti sabbattha, momūhāhetuvajjite;

Adhimokkho vicikicchā-pañcaviññāṇavajjite.

Desire is excluded from consciousness rooted in delusion and from rootless consciousness. Decision is excluded from consciousness accompanied by doubt and from the ten sense-consciousnesses.

302.

302.

Chasaṭṭhi [M 0.0027][V 0.0030] pañcapaññāsa, sattati ceva soḷasa;

Vīsatekādasevātha, pakiṇṇakavivajjitā.

The miscellaneous factors are excluded respectively from sixty-six, fifty-five, seventy, sixteen, twenty, and eleven types of consciousness.

303.

303.

Mānasā pañcapaññāsa, savitakkā chasaṭṭhi ca;

Savicārekapaññāsa, sappītikamanā tathā.

Fifty-five types of consciousness are accompanied by initial application, sixty-six by sustained application, and fifty-one are likewise accompanied by rapture.

304.

304.

Tesattati savīriyā, sachandekūnasattati;

Sādhimokkhā pavuccanti, aṭṭhasattati mānasā.

Seventy-three types of consciousness are with energy, sixty-nine with desire; and seventy-eight minds are said to be with decision.

305.

305.

Paññāppamaññāviratī, hitvā ekūnasaṭṭhisu;

Pāpāhetukamuttesu, saddhādekūnavīsati.

Excluding wisdom, the illimitables, and the abstinences, the nineteen factors beginning with faith arise in the fifty-nine types of beautiful consciousness.

306.

306.

Dvihetukāhetupāpavajjitesu samāsato;

Paññā tu jāyate sattacattālīsesu sabbathā.

In brief, wisdom arises in the forty-seven types of consciousness that remain when the unwholesome, the rootless, and the two-rooted types are excluded.

307.

307.

Mahākriyākāmapuñña-rūpajjhānesu jāyare;

Appamaññāṭṭhavīsesu, hitvā jhānaṃ tu pañcamaṃ.

The illimitables arise in twenty-eight types of consciousness—namely, in the sense-sphere wholesome and great functional consciousness, and in the fine-material jhanas—but they are excluded from the fifth jhana.

308.

308.

Lokuttaresu sabbattha, saheva viratittayaṃ;

Kāmapuññesu sambhoti, yathāsambhavato visuṃ.

In all supramundane consciousness, the three abstinences arise together. In sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, they arise separately, according to the occasion.

309.

309.

Viratīappamaññāsu, pañcasvapi yathārahaṃ;

Kadācideva sambhoti, ekekova na cekato.

Among the five factors—the abstinences and the illimitables—each arises only occasionally and one at a time, as is appropriate, not all together.

310.

310.

Ahirīkamanottappaṃ, mohauddhaccameva ca;

Pāpasādhāraṇā nāma, cattāro pāpasambhavā.

Shamelessness, lack of moral dread, delusion, and restlessness—these four are called the unwholesome universals, as they arise in all unwholesome consciousness.

311.

311.

Lobho ca lobhamūlesu, diṭṭhiyuttesu diṭṭhi ca;

Māno diṭṭhiviyuttesu, diṭṭhimānā na cekato.

Greed arises in consciousness rooted in greed, and wrong view in consciousness associated with wrong view. Conceit arises in consciousness dissociated from wrong view; wrong view and conceit do not arise together.

312.

312.

Dosamūlesu doso ca, issā macchariyaṃ tathā;

Kukkuccamiti cattāro, vicikicchā tu kaṅkhite.

In consciousnesses rooted in hatred arise hatred, envy, avarice, and worry. Doubt, however, arises in the consciousness accompanied by doubt.

313.

313.

Saheva thinamiddhaṃ tu, sasaṅkhāresu pañcasu;

Iti cuddasa sāvajjā, sāvajjesveva nicchitā.

Sloth and torpor, however, arise together in the five types of prompted unwholesome consciousness. Thus the fourteen blameworthy factors are determined to arise only in blameworthy consciousnesses.

314.

314.

Māno [M 0.0028][V 0.0031] ca thinamiddhañca, saha vātha visuṃ na vā;

Issāmaccherakukkuccā, aññamaññaṃ visuṃ na vāti.

Conceit, and sloth and torpor, may or may not arise together; envy, avarice, and worry do not arise together with one another.

Iti cetasikavibhāge cetasikasampayogakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the section on the association of mental factors in the analysis of mental factors.

Aṭṭhamo paricchedo.

Chapter Eight.

Navamo paricchedo

Chapter Nine

9. Cetasikasaṅgahakathā

9. The Discourse on the Combination of Mental Factors

315.

315.

Satta sādhāraṇā ceva, cha dhammā ca pakiṇṇakā;

Saddhādi pañcavīseti, aṭṭhatiṃsa samissitā.

The seven universals, the six occasional factors, and the twenty-five beautiful factors beginning with faith—these thirty-eight are combined.

316.

316.

Kāmāvacarapuññesu, labbhanti paṭhamadvaye;

Sattatiṃseva dutiye, paññāmattavivajjitā.

In the first pair of sense-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, thirty-eight factors are found. In the second pair, thirty-seven are found, with only wisdom being excluded.

317.

317.

Tatiye ca yathāvuttā, pītimattavivajjitā;

Chattiṃseva catutthamhi, paññāpītidvayaṃ vinā.

In the third pair, there are thirty-seven factors, with only rapture being excluded. In the fourth pair, there are thirty-six, without the pair of wisdom and rapture.

318.

318.

Mahākriyāsu yujjanti, hitvā viratiyo tathā;

Pañcatiṃsa catuttiṃsadvayaṃ tettiṃsakaṃ kamā.

In the great functional consciousnesses, excluding the abstinences, there are conjoined, in sequence: thirty-five factors, two sets of thirty-four, and thirty-three.

319.

319.

Ṭhapetvā appamaññā ca, mahāpākesu yojitā;

Tettiṃsā ceva dvattiṃsadvayekattiṃsakaṃ kamā.

Setting aside the illimitables and applied to the great resultants, there are in sequence: thirty-three factors, two sets of thirty-two, and thirty-one.

320.

320.

Appamaññā gahetvāna, hitvā viratiyo tathā;

Pañcatiṃseva paṭhame, rūpāvacaramānase.

Including the illimitables and excluding the abstinences, there are thirty-five factors in the first fine-material sphere consciousness.

321.

321.

Vitakkaṃ dutiye hitvā, vicārañca tato paraṃ;

Catutthe pana pītiñca, appamaññañca pañcame.

Initial application is abandoned in the second, sustained application in the one thereafter, rapture in the fourth, and the illimitables in the fifth.

322.

322.

Yathāvuttapakārāva[V 0.0032], catuttiṃsa yathākkamaṃ;

Tettiṃsa ceva dvattiṃsa, samatiṃsañca labbhare.

Following the method just stated, the factors obtained are, in sequence: thirty-four, thirty-three, thirty-two, and thirty.

323.

323.

Pañcamena samānā ca, ṭhapetvāruppamānasā;

Bhūmārammaṇabhedañca, aṅgānañca paṇītataṃ.

The immaterial sphere consciousnesses are the same as the fifth jhāna, except for the difference in plane and object, and the greater sublimity of their factors.

324.

324.

Appamaññā [M 0.0029] ṭhapetvāna, gahetvā viratittayaṃ;

Chattiṃsānuttare honti, paṭhamajjhānamānase.

Setting aside the illimitables and taking up the three abstinences, there are thirty-six factors in the supramundane first jhāna consciousness.

325.

325.

Vitakkaṃ dutiye hitvā, vicārañca tato paraṃ;

Pītiṃ hitvā catutthe ca, pañcamepi ca sabbathā.

Initial application is abandoned in the second, sustained application thereafter, rapture in the fourth, and all of them likewise in the fifth.

326.

326.

Yathāvuttappakārāva, pañcatiṃsa yathākkamaṃ;

Catuttiṃsañca tettiṃsa, tathā tettiṃsa cāpare.

In the aforesaid manner, there are successively thirty-five, thirty-four, thirty-three, and likewise thirty-three for the last.

327.

327.

Evaṃ bāvīsadhā bhedo, anavajjesu saṅgaho;

Ekūnasaṭṭhicittesu, aṭṭhatiṃsānamīrito.

Thus the division is in twenty-two ways. The classification of the thirty-eight beautiful mental factors in the fifty-nine blameless types of consciousness has been stated.

328.

328.

Viratī appamaññā ca, gahetvā pana sabbaso;

Ekamekaṃ gahetvā ca, paccakkhāya ca sabbathā.

This is done by including the abstinences and illimitables all together, by including them one by one, and by excluding them entirely.

329.

329.

Kāmesu sattadhā puññe, catudhā ca kriye tathā;

Rūpajjhānacatukke ca, kattabboyampi saṅgaho.

This classification should be made sevenfold in the sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, likewise fourfold in the functional, and also in the fourfold form-sphere jhānas.

330.

330.

Iminā panupāyena, samasattati bhedato;

Anavajjesu viññeyyo, cittuppādesu saṅgaho.

By this method, the classification in the arisings of blameless consciousness should be understood as having seventy divisions.

331.

331.

Iti sabbappakārena, anavajjavinicchayaṃ;

Ñatvā yojeyya medhāvī, sāvajjesu ca saṅgahaṃ.

Thus, having known in every way the analysis of the blameless, the wise one should also apply the classification to the blameworthy.

332.

332.

Satta sādhāraṇā ceva, cha dhammā ca pakiṇṇakā;

Cattāro pāpasāmaññā, dhammā sattarasevime.

Seven are the universals, six are the occasionals, and four are common to the unwholesome; these are seventeen factors.

333.

333.

Ekūnavīsāsaṅkhāre, paṭhame lobhadiṭṭhiyā;

Dutiye lobhamānena, yathāvuttā ca tattakā.

In the first unprompted consciousness rooted in greed associated with wrong view, there are nineteen factors. In the second, associated with conceit, there are just as many.

334.

334.

Aṭṭhārasa [V 0.0033] vinā pītiṃ, tatiye lobhadiṭṭhiyā;

Catutthepi vinā pītiṃ, lobhamānena tattakā.

In the third type, associated with greed and wrong view, there are eighteen, without joy. In the fourth also, associated with greed and conceit, there are just as many, without joy.

335.

335.

Paṭighe ca vinā pītiṃ, asaṅkhāre tatheva te;

Labbhanti dosakukkucca-macchariyāhi vīsati.

In the unprompted consciousness rooted in aversion, which is without joy, twenty factors are found, including hatred, worry, and stinginess.

336.

336.

Asaṅkhāresu vuttā ca, sasaṅkhāresu pañcadhā;

Thinamiddhenekavīsa, vīsa dvevīsatikkamā.

As stated for the unprompted types, so for the five prompted types: with the addition of sloth and torpor, the totals are respectively twenty-one, twenty, and twenty-two.

337.

337.

Chandaṃ [M 0.0030] pītiñca uddhacce, hitvā pañcadaseva te;

Hitvā vimokkhaṃ kaṅkhañca, gahetvā kaṅkhite tathā.

In the consciousness with restlessness, abandoning desire and joy, there are fifteen factors. Likewise, in the one with doubt, abandoning resolve and including doubt, there are fifteen.

338.

338.

Sattavīsatidhammānaṃ, iti dvādasa saṅgahā;

Dvādasāpuññacittesu, viññātabbā vibhāvinā.

Thus, the twelvefold classification of the twenty-seven factors in the twelve unwholesome types of consciousness should be understood by the discerning one.

339.

339.

Hitvā chāniyate dhamme, gahetvā ca yathārahaṃ;

Catuttiṃsāpi viññeyyā, saṅgahā tattha viññunā.

By excluding and including the six variable factors as is appropriate, thirty-four classifications are also to be understood by the wise.

340.

340.

Dvādasākusalesveva, ñatvā saṅgahamuttaraṃ;

Ñeyyāhetukacittesu, saṅgahaṃ kamato kathaṃ?

Having known the further classification in the twelve unwholesome types of consciousness, how is the classification in the rootless types of consciousness to be known in sequence?

341.

341.

Satta sādhāraṇā chandavajjitā ca pakiṇṇakā;

Hasituppādacittamhi, dvādaseva pakāsitā.

In the smile-producing consciousness, just twelve factors are declared: the seven universals and the occasionals excluding desire.

342.

342.

Voṭṭhabbe ca vinā pītiṃ, vīriyaṃ sukhatīraṇe;

Ekādasa yathāvuttā, dhammā dvīsupi desitā.

In the determining consciousness, without joy, and in the pleasant investigating consciousness, without energy, eleven factors as stated are taught in both.

343.

343.

Manodhātuttike ceva, upekkhātīraṇadvaye;

Dasa honti yathāvuttā, hitvā vīriyapītiyo.

In the triad of mind-elements and in the two investigating consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, there are ten factors as stated, excluding energy and joy.

344.

344.

Satta sādhāraṇā eva, pañcaviññāṇasambhavā;

Iccāhetukacittesu, pañcadhā saṅgaho ṭhito.

Just the seven universals arise in the five sense-consciousnesses. Thus, in the rootless types of consciousness, the classification is established in five ways.

345.

345.

Iti cetasike dhamme, cittesu gaṇite puna;

Cittena saha saṅgayha, gaṇeyyāpi ca paṇḍito.

Thus, when the mental factors in the types of consciousness have been enumerated, the wise one should also count them by combining them together with the consciousness.

346.

346.

Aṭṭhatiṃsāti [V 0.0034] ye vuttā, cittena saha te puna;

Ekūnacattālīseti, sabbatthekādhikaṃ naye.

Those factors which were stated as thirty-eight become thirty-nine when taken together with consciousness. In every case, one should infer one more.

347.

347.

Bāvīsevaṃ dasa dve ca, pañca ceti yathārahaṃ;

Saṅgahā sampayuttānaṃ, tālīsekūnakā kathā.

Thus, as is appropriate, there are twenty-two, ten, two, and five classifications of the associated factors. The account totals thirty-nine.

348.

348.

Vitakko ca vicāro ca, pīti paññā tathā pana;

Appamaññā viratīti, nava dhammā yathārahaṃ.

Initial application, sustained application, joy, wisdom, and also the immeasurables and the abstinences—these nine factors vary according to the case.

349.

349.

Gahetabbāpanetabbā, bhavanti anavajjake;

Parivatteti sabbattha, vedanā tu yathārahaṃ.

In the blameless types of consciousness, they are to be included or excluded. Feeling, however, varies everywhere as is appropriate.

350.

350.

Chandādhimokkhavīriyā[M 0.0031], saddhādekūnavīsati;

Phassādayo chaḷevāti, na calantaṭṭhavīsati.

Zeal, resolve, and energy; the nineteen beautiful factors beginning with faith; and the six beginning with contact—thus, twenty-eight do not waver.

351.

351.

Teraseva tu sāvajje, chaḷevāhetumānase;

Na calanti dasa aññe, cuddasā cha ca sambhavāti.

Thirteen factors in the blameworthy, and six in the rootless mind, do not waver. Ten others, fourteen, and six arise.

Iti cetasikavibhāge cetasikasaṅgahakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the discussion on the compendium of mental factors in the Analysis of Mental Factors.

Navamo paricchedo.

The Ninth Chapter.

Dasamo paricchedo

The Tenth Chapter.

10. Pabhedakathā

10. Discussion on Divisions.

352.

352.

Ekuppādā nirodhā ca, ekālambaṇavatthukā;

Sahagatā sahajātā, saṃsaṭṭhā sahavuttino.

Arising and ceasing together, having a single object and base; they are associated, co-nascent, conjoined, and co-existent.

353.

353.

Tepaññāsa paniccete, sampayuttā yathārahaṃ;

Cittacetasikā dhammā, aṭṭhārasavidhāpi ca.

These fifty-three factors—consciousness and mental factors—are associated as is appropriate, and are also of eighteen kinds.

354.

354.

Ekadhā [V 0.0035] chabbidhā ceva, catudhā sattadhā ṭhitā;

Cittuppādapabhedena, bhinditabbā vibhāvinā.

Established as onefold, sixfold, fourfold, and sevenfold, they should be analyzed by the discerning one according to the divisions in the arising of consciousness.

355.

355.

Aṭṭha dhammāvinibbhogā, bhinnāsīti navuttarā;

Sattasataṃ dasa dve ca, sabbe honti samissitā.

The eight inseparable factors, divided among the eighty-nine types of consciousness, become seven hundred and twelve; all are intermingled.

356.

356.

Santīraṇamanodhātu, sitavoṭṭhabbanā tathā;

Apuññā kāmapuññā ca, mahāpākā mahākriyā.

Investigating consciousness, mind-element, smile-producing and determining consciousness; likewise, unwholesome, sense-sphere wholesome, great resultants, and great functionals.

357.

357.

Paṭhamajjhānadhammā ca, lokuttaramahaggatā;

Pañcapaññāsa sabbepi, vitakkā honti bheditā.

The factors of the first jhāna, both supramundane and sublime—all fifty-five types of consciousness—are distinguished by the presence of initial application.

358.

358.

Vicārāpi ca teyeva, dutiyajjhānanāmakā;

Ekādasāpare ceti, chasaṭṭhi paridīpitā.

Those same fifty-five types of consciousness are also associated with sustained application; with eleven others called second jhāna, sixty-six are thus explained.

359.

359.

Apuññā kāmapuññā ca, mahāpākā mahākriyā;

Catukkā ceva cattāro, sitañca sukhatīraṇaṃ.

The unwholesome, the sense-sphere wholesome, the great resultants, and the great functionals—four from each of these four groups; and the smile-producing and the pleasant investigating consciousness.

360.

360.

Paṭhamāditikajjhānā[M 0.0032], lokuttaramahaggatā;

Iccevamekapaññāsa, pītiyo honti sabbathā.

The first three absorptions, both supramundane and sublime; thus in all ways there are fifty-one kinds of joy.

361.

361.

Sitavoṭṭhabbanā dve ca, sāvajjā cānavajjakā;

Bhinnamevaṃ tu vīriyaṃ, tesattatividhaṃ bhave.

Smiling and determining, these two, the blameworthy and the blameless; thus energy, being divided, is of seventy-three kinds.

362.

362.

Sāvajjā cānavajjā ca, momūhadvayavajjitā;

Chandā bhavanti sabbepi, saṭṭhibhedā navuttarā.

Volition is present in all blameworthy and blameless consciousnesses, excluding the two rooted in delusion; thus it is of sixty-nine divisions.

363.

363.

Santīraṇamanodhātu, sitavoṭṭhabbanā tathā;

Sāvajjā cānavajjā ca, vicikicchāvivajjitā.

Investigating consciousness, mind-element, likewise smiling and determining; the blameworthy and the blameless, excluding that associated with doubt.

364.

364.

Adhimokkhā paniccevaṃ, aṭṭhasattati bheditā;

Tisataṃ navuti dve ca, bhinnā honti pakiṇṇakā.

Thus decision is divided into seventy-eight kinds. The miscellaneous factors are divided into three hundred and ninety-two.

365.

365.

Ekūnasaṭṭhi vā honti, saddhādekūnavīsati;

Sahassañca satañcekaṃ, ekavīsañca sabbathā.

Or there are fifty-nine. Faith and the others are nineteen. Altogether, there are one thousand, one hundred, and twenty-one.

366.

366.

Ñāṇena [V 0.0036] sampayuttā ca, kāme dvādasadhāpare;

Pañcatiṃsāti paññāpi, sattatālīsadhā kathā.

Associated with knowledge, there are twelve in the sense sphere; wisdom is also in thirty-five others. Thus it is said to be forty-sevenfold.

367.

367.

Rūpajjhānacatukkā ca, kāmapuññā mahākriyā;

Aṭṭhavīsappamaññevaṃ, chappaññāsa bhavanti ca.

In the four form-sphere jhānas, in sense-sphere wholesome and great functional consciousness, thus the illimitables are twenty-eightfold, and come to be fifty-six.

368.

368.

Anuttarā kāmapuññā, tisso viratiyo pana;

Honti soḷasadhā bhinnā, aṭṭhatālīsa piṇḍitā.

In supramundane and sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, the three abstinences are divided into sixteen kinds, totaling forty-eight.

369.

369.

Pañcavīsānavajjevaṃ, sampayuttā catubbidhā;

Sahassadvisatañceva, dvi ca sattati bhedato.

Thus the twenty-five blameless factors are associated in four ways; by division, they are one thousand, two hundred, and seventy-two.

370.

370.

Cattāro pāpasāmaññā, bhinnā dvādasadhā pana;

Aṭṭhatālīsadhā honti, te sabbe paripiṇḍitā.

The four factors common to all unwholesome states are divided twelvefold; all of them grouped together become forty-eight.

371.

371.

Lobho panaṭṭhadhā bhinno, thinamiddhañca pañcadhā;

Catudhā diṭṭhimāno ca, catudhā diṭṭhiyo visuṃ.

Greed, however, is divided eightfold; sloth and torpor fivefold; wrong view and conceit fourfold; and wrong views separately fourfold.

372.

372.

Dvidhā dosādicattāro, vicikicchekadhāti ca;

Sāvajjā sattadhā vuttā, bhinnāsīti tikuttarā.

The four beginning with hatred are twofold, and doubt is onefold. The blameworthy factors are said to be sevenfold, divided into eighty-three.

373.

373.

Iccaṭṭhārasadhā [M 0.0033] vuttā, tepaññāsāpi bhedato;

Dvisahassañca tu sataṃ, bhavantekūnasaṭṭhi ca.

Thus eighteen are spoken of, and fifty-three by division; they become two thousand, one hundred, and fifty-nine.

374.

374.

Vitakkavicārapītisukhopekkhāsu pañcasu;

Bhinditvā jhānabhedena, gahetabbā anuttarā.

Regarding the five—initial application, sustained application, rapture, happiness, and equanimity—the supramundane should be understood by analyzing them according to the divisions of jhāna.

375.

375.

Aññatra pana sabbattha, natthi bhedappayojanaṃ;

Aṭṭheva kasmā gayhanti, abhedenāti lakkhaye.

But elsewhere, in every case, there is no purpose in making divisions. Why are only eight taken? This should be understood as being without distinction.

376.

376.

Paṭhamādicatujjhānā, lokuttaramahaggatā;

Iccekamekadasadhā, catutālīsa piṇḍitā.

The first four jhānas, the supramundane, and the sublime; thus each is elevenfold, totaling forty-four.

377.

377.

Tevīsa pañcamā ceti, sattasaṭṭhi samissitā;

Appanā tattha sabbāpi, aṭṭhapaññāsa dīpitā.

Twenty-three of the fifth, making sixty-seven when combined. All the absorption concentration there is shown as fifty-eight.

378.

378.

Pañcatiṃseva [V 0.0037] saṅkhepā, lokuttaramahaggatā;

Appanā tattha sabbāpi, chabbīsati pakāsitā.

In brief, thirty-five are the supramundane and the sublime. All the absorption concentration there is declared as twenty-six.

379.

379.

Iddhividhaṃ dibbasotaṃ, cetopariyanāmakā;

Pubbenivāsānussati, dibbacakkhūti pañcadhā.

The modes of psychic power, the divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, and the divine eye—these five.

380.

380.

Abhiññāñāṇamīrenti, rūpāvacarapañcamā;

Kusalañca kriyā ceti, bheditaṃ duvidhampi ca.

They declare this as the knowledge of direct knowing, based on the fifth form-sphere jhāna; it is divided into two kinds: wholesome and functional.

381.

381.

Taṃ dvayampi sammissetvā, pañcābhiññā ca lokiyā;

Āsavakkhayañāṇañca, chaḷabhiññā pavuccare.

The five mundane higher knowledges and the knowledge of the destruction of the taints are together declared as the six higher knowledges.

382.

382.

Lokiyā ca dasābhiññā, bhinditvā kusalakriyā;

Sattasattati jhānāni, aṭṭhasaṭṭhi panappanā.

The ten mundane higher knowledges are divided into wholesome and functional. There are seventy-seven jhānas, but sixty-eight absorptions.

383.

383.

Sattasattati cittāni, catupaññāsa sabbathā;

Pacitāni ca cittāni, ekatiṃsasataṃ siyunti.

Seventy-seven cittas, and fifty-four in all; and the accumulated cittas would be one hundred and thirty-one.

Iti cetasikavibhāge pabhedakathā niṭṭhitā.

Thus ends the discussion on the divisions in the analysis of mental factors.

Dasamo paricchedo.

The Tenth Chapter.

Ekādasamo paricchedo

The Eleventh Chapter.

11. Rāsisarūpakathā

11. Discussion on the Nature of the Groups

384.

384.

Sabbaṃ [M 0.0034] sabhāvasāmañña-visesena yathārahaṃ;

Gatarāsivasenātha, aṭṭhārasavidhaṃ kathaṃ.

Now, by way of the groups that have treated all things appropriately according to their general and specific nature, how is the eighteenfold classification explained?

385.

385.

Phassapañcakarāsī ca, jhānindriyamathāpare;

Maggabalahetukamma-pathalokiyarāsayo.

The group of five beginning with contact, then the jhāna factors and faculties; the groups of path, power, root, kamma-patha, and the mundane.

386.

386.

Niravajjā [V 0.0038] cha passaddhi-ādikā ca satīmatā;

Yuganandhā ca samathā, tathā yevāpanāti ca.

The blameless group, the group of six beginning with tranquility, the mindfulness group; the paired group, the serenity group, and likewise the attainment group.

387.

387.

Phasso ca vedanā saññā, cetanā cittameva ca;

Phassapañcakarāsīti, pañca dhammā pakāsitā.

Contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness: these five phenomena are declared as the 'group of five beginning with contact'.

388.

388.

Vitakko ca vicāro ca, pīti cekaggatā tathā;

Sukhaṃ dukkhamupekkhāti, satta jhānaṅganāmakā.

Initial application, sustained application, rapture, and one-pointedness, likewise happiness, suffering, and equanimity—these seven are named the jhāna factors.

389.

389.

Saddhindriyañca vīriyaṃ, sati ceva samādhi ca;

Paññā catubbidhā vuttā, mano pañcāpi vedanā.

The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration; wisdom is said to be fourfold, mind is a faculty, and feeling is fivefold.

390.

390.

Jīvitindriyamekanti, cakkhādīni ca sattadhā;

Bāvīsatindriyā nāma, dhammā soḷasa desitā.

The life faculty is one, and there are seven beginning with the eye. They are named the twenty-two faculties, but are taught as sixteen phenomena.

391.

391.

Ādimagge anaññāta-ññassāmītindriyaṃ bhave;

Majjhe aññindriyaṃ ante, aññātāvindriyanti ca.

On the initial path, there is the faculty 'I shall come to know the unknown.' In the middle, there is the faculty of final knowledge. At the end, there is the faculty of one who has final knowledge.

392.

392.

Paññānuttaracittesu, honti tīṇindriyānipi;

Tihetukesu sesesu, ekaṃ paññindriyaṃ mataṃ.

In the supramundane consciousnesses, there are three faculties of wisdom; in the remaining three-rooted consciousnesses, the single faculty of wisdom is reckoned.

393.

393.

Sukhaṃ dukkhindriyañceva, somanassindriyaṃ tathā;

Domanassamupekkhāti, pañcadhā vedanā kathā.

The faculty of pleasure and the faculty of pain, likewise the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity—thus feeling is explained in five ways.

394.

394.

Rūpārūpavasā dvedhā, jīvitindriyamekakaṃ;

Cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyitthipurisindriyā.

The single life faculty is twofold, by way of its material and mental aspects. The faculties are: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, the female faculty, and the male faculty.

395.

395.

Tattha jīvitarūpañca, aṭṭhettha na tu gayhare;

Tasmā nāmindriyāneva, dasapañca viniddise.

Herein, the eight material faculties, including the material life faculty, are not to be taken. Therefore, one should point out only the fifteen mental faculties.

396.

396.

Sammādiṭṭhi [M 0.0035] ca saṅkappo, vāyāmo viratittayaṃ;

Sammāsati samādhi ca, micchādiṭṭhi ca dhammato.

Right view and right intention, effort, and the three abstinences; right mindfulness and concentration, and wrong view as a factor.

397.

397.

Maggaṅgāni navetāni, dvādasāpi yato dvidhā;

Sammāmicchāti saṅkappo, vāyāmo ca samādhi ca.

These nine are path factors, and also twelve, since they are twofold: right and wrong intention, effort, and concentration.

398.

398.

Lokapāladukañceva[V 0.0039], hirottappamathāparaṃ;

Ahirīkamanottappaṃ, dukaṃ lokavināsakaṃ.

The pair of guardians of the world, namely, conscience and moral dread; and the other pair, shamelessness and lack of moral dread, are the destroyers of the world.

399.

399.

Pañca saddhādayo ceti, baladhammā naveritā;

Kaṇhasukkavasenāpi, paṭipakkhe akampiyā.

The five beginning with faith, and others, are declared as nine powers; by way of dark and bright, they are unshakeable by their opposites.

400.

400.

Cha hetū heturāsimhi,

Lobhālobhādikā tikā;

Momūhe kaṅkhituddhaccā,

Tattha vuttāti aṭṭhadhā.
